question: A company is building a web-based AI application by using Amazon SageMaker. The application will provide the following capabilities and features: ML experimentation, training, a central model registry, model deployment, and model monitoring. The application must ensure secure and isolated use of training data during the ML lifecycle. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. The company needs to use the central model registry to manage different versions of models in the application. Which action will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create a separate Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository for each model.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and unique tags for each model version.
mcqs.C: Use the SageMaker Model Registry and model groups to catalog the models.
mcqs.D: Use the SageMaker Model Registry and unique tags for each model version.

explanation: SageMaker Model Registry with model groups provides built-in versioning and metadata management for ML models with minimal operational overhead.

question: A company is building a web-based AI application by using Amazon SageMaker. The application will provide the following capabilities and features: ML experimentation, training, a central model registry, model deployment, and model monitoring. The application must ensure secure and isolated use of training data during the ML lifecycle. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. The company is experimenting with consecutive training jobs. How can the company MINIMIZE infrastructure startup times for these jobs?

mcqs.A: Use Managed Spot Training.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker managed warm pools.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Training Compiler.
mcqs.D: Use the SageMaker distributed data parallelism (SMDDP) library.

explanation: SageMaker managed warm pools reduce infrastructure startup times by retaining provisioned infrastructure between training jobs.

question: A company is building a web-based AI application by using Amazon SageMaker. The application will provide the following capabilities and features: ML experimentation, training, a central model registry, model deployment, and model monitoring. The application must ensure secure and isolated use of training data during the ML lifecycle. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. The company must implement a manual approval-based workflow to ensure that only approved models can be deployed to production endpoints.

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Experiments to facilitate the approval process during model registration.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking on the central model registry. Create tracking entities for the approval process.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to evaluate the performance of the model and to manage the approval.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Pipelines. When a model version is registered, use the AWS SDK to change the approval status to Approved.

explanation: SageMaker Pipelines with Model Registry enables manual approval gates before production deployment.

question: A company is building a web-based AI application by using Amazon SageMaker. The application will provide the following capabilities and features: ML experimentation, training, a central model registry, model deployment, and model monitoring. The application must ensure secure and isolated use of training data during the ML lifecycle. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. The company needs to run an on-demand workflow to monitor bias drift for models that are deployed to real-time endpoints from the application. Which action will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Configure the application to invoke an AWS Lambda function that runs a SageMaker Clarify job.
mcqs.B: Invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull the sagemaker-model-monitor-analyzer built-in SageMaker image.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue Data Quality to monitor bias.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker notebooks to compare the bias.

explanation: SageMaker Clarify can be used to monitor bias drift. Invoking a Lambda function to run a SageMaker Clarify job allows for on-demand bias drift analysis.

question: A company is developing a fraud detection model on AWS. The training dataset includes transaction logs, customer profiles, and tables from an on-premises MySQL database. The transaction logs and customer profiles are stored in Amazon S3. The dataset has a class imbalance that affects the learning of the model's algorithm. Additionally, many of the features have interdependencies. The algorithm is not capturing all the desired underlying patterns in the data. Which AWS service or feature can aggregate the data from the various data sources?

mcqs.A: Amazon EMR Spark jobs
mcqs.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
mcqs.C: Amazon DynamoDB
mcqs.D: AWS Lake Formation

explanation: AWS Lake Formation can aggregate data from various sources including Amazon S3, MySQL database, and more.

question: A company is developing a fraud detection model on AWS. The training dataset includes transaction logs, customer profiles, and tables from an on-premises MySQL database. The transaction logs and customer profiles are stored in Amazon S3. After the data is aggregated, the ML engineer must implement a solution to automatically detect anomalies in the data and to visualize the result. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Athena to automatically detect the anomalies and to visualize the result.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to automatically detect the anomalies. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the result.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to automatically detect the anomalies and to visualize the result.
mcqs.D: Use AWS Batch to automatically detect the anomalies. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the result.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler can be used to detect anomalies and visualize results, making it a suitable choice for this task.

question: A company is developing a fraud detection model on AWS. The training dataset includes transaction logs, customer profiles, and tables from an on-premises MySQL database. The training dataset includes categorical data and numerical data. The ML engineer must prepare the training dataset to maximize the accuracy of the model. Which action will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use AWS Glue to transform the categorical data into numerical data.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue to transform the numerical data into categorical data.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to transform the categorical data into numerical data.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to transform the numerical data into categorical data.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler provides a faster and more efficient way to prepare data for machine learning compared to AWS Glue.

question: A company is developing a fraud detection model on AWS. The ML engineer must resolve the issue of the imbalanced data before training the model. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Athena to identify patterns that contribute to the imbalance. Adjust the dataset accordingly.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic built-in algorithms to process the imbalanced dataset.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew built-in features to oversample the minority class.
mcqs.D: Use the Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler balance data operation to oversample the minority class.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler provides a simple and efficient way to balance data, requiring the least operational effort.

question: A company is developing a fraud detection model on AWS. The ML engineer needs to use an Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithm to train the model. Which algorithm should the ML engineer use to meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: LightGBM
mcqs.B: Linear learner
mcqs.C: K-means clustering
mcqs.D: Neural Topic Model (NTM)

explanation: SageMaker built-in Linear Learner can be used for fraud detection tasks and is a suitable algorithm for this use case.
errors_found: Provided explanation mentions XGBoost but answer option is LightGBM, and correct answer should be B

question: A company has deployed an XGBoost prediction model in production to predict if a customer is likely to cancel a subscription. The company uses Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to detect deviations in the F1 score. During a baseline analysis of model quality, the company recorded a threshold for the F1 score. After several months of no change, the model's F1 score decreases significantly. What could be the reason for the reduced F1 score?

mcqs.A: Concept drift occurred in the underlying customer data that was used for predictions.
mcqs.B: The model was not sufficiently complex to capture all the patterns in the original baseline data.
mcqs.C: The original baseline data had a data quality issue of missing values.
mcqs.D: Incorrect ground truth labels were provided to Model Monitor during the calculation of the baseline.

explanation: Concept drift refers to a change in the relationship between the target variable and the predictor variables over time. This can cause a model's performance to degrade, as the model is no longer accurately capturing the underlying patterns in the data. In this case, concept drift in the customer data could be the reason for the reduced F1 score.

question: A company has a team of data scientists who use Amazon SageMaker notebook instances to test ML models. When the data scientists need new permissions, the company attaches the permissions to each individual role that was created during the creation of the SageMaker notebook instance. The company needs to centralize management of the team's permissions. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Create a single IAM role that has the necessary permissions. Attach the role to each notebook instance that the team uses.
mcqs.B: Create a single IAM group. Add the data scientists to the group. Associate the group with each notebook instance that the team uses.
mcqs.C: Create a single IAM user. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed IAM policy to the user. Configure each notebook instance to use the IAM user.
mcqs.D: Create a single IAM group. Add the data scientists to the group. Create an IAM role. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed IAM policy to the role. Associate the role with the group. Associate the group with each notebook instance that the team uses.

explanation: Creating a single IAM role with necessary permissions and attaching it to each notebook instance centralizes permission management. This approach eliminates the need to update individual roles. It ensures that all data scientists have the required permissions.

question: An ML engineer needs to use an ML model to predict the price of apartments in a specific location. Which metric should the ML engineer use to evaluate the model's performance?

mcqs.A: Accuracy
mcqs.B: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
mcqs.C: F1 score
mcqs.D: Mean absolute error (MAE)

explanation: For predicting continuous numeric output like apartment prices, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is a suitable metric as it measures the average difference between predicted and actual values.

question: An ML engineer has trained a neural network using stochastic gradient descent (SGD). The neural network performs poorly on the test set. The values for training loss and validation loss remain high and show an oscillating pattern. The values decrease for a few epochs and then increase for a few epochs before repeating the same cycle. What should the ML engineer do to improve the training process?

mcqs.A: Introduce early stopping.
mcqs.B: Increase the size of the test set.
mcqs.C: Increase the learning rate.
mcqs.D: Decrease the learning rate.

explanation: Loss oscillation during SGD training indicates the learning rate is too high. Decreasing it allows smoother, more stable convergence.

question: An ML engineer needs to process thousands of existing CSV objects and new CSV objects that are uploaded. The CSV objects are stored in a central Amazon S3 bucket and have the same number of columns. One of the columns is a transaction date. The ML engineer must query the data based on the transaction date. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use an Amazon Athena CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) statement to create a table based on the transaction date from data in the central S3 bucket. Query the objects from the table.
mcqs.B: Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Set up S3 replication from the central S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Object Lambda to query the objects based on transaction date.
mcqs.C: Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Use AWS Glue for Apache Spark to create a job to query the CSV objects based on transaction date. Configure the job to store the results in the new S3 bucket. Query the objects from the new S3 bucket.
mcqs.D: Create a new S3 bucket for processed data. Use Amazon Data Firehose to transfer the data from the central S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket. Configure Firehose to run an AWS Lambda function to query the data based on transaction date.

explanation: Amazon Athena with CTAS queries S3 data directly using serverless SQL, providing the least operational overhead for filtering and partitioning CSV objects.

question: A company has a large, unstructured dataset. The dataset includes many duplicate records across several key attributes. Which solution on AWS will detect duplicates in the dataset with the LEAST code development?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Mechanical Turk jobs to detect duplicates.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon QuickSight ML Insights to build a custom deduplication model.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to pre-process and detect duplicates.
mcqs.D: Use the AWS Glue FindMatches transform to detect duplicates.

explanation: AWS Glue FindMatches transform detects duplicates with minimal code development, ideal for fuzzy deduplication.

question: A company needs to run a batch data-processing job on Amazon EC2 instances. The job will run during the weekend and will take 90 minutes to finish running. The processing can handle interruptions. The company will run the job every weekend for the next 6 months. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

mcqs.A: Spot Instances
mcqs.B: Reserved Instances
mcqs.C: On-Demand Instances
mcqs.D: Dedicated Instances

explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings over On-Demand pricing and are ideal for fault-tolerant batch jobs that can handle interruptions.

question: An ML engineer has an Amazon Comprehend custom model in Account A in the us-east-1 Region. The ML engineer needs to copy the model to Account B in the same Region. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon S3 to make a copy of the model. Transfer the copy to Account B.
mcqs.B: Create a resource-based IAM policy. Use the Amazon Comprehend ImportModel API operation to copy the model to Account B.
mcqs.C: Use AWS DataSync to replicate the model from Account A to Account B.
mcqs.D: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between Account A and Account B to transfer the model.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides an ImportModel API to copy models across accounts in the same region.

question: An ML engineer is training a simple neural network model. The ML engineer tracks the performance of the model over time on a validation dataset. The model's performance improves substantially at first and then degrades after a specific number of epochs. Which solutions will mitigate this problem? (Choose two.)

mcqs.A: Enable early stopping on the model.
mcqs.B: Increase dropout in the layers.
mcqs.C: Increase the number of layers.
mcqs.D: Increase the number of neurons.

explanation: Early stopping and dropout mitigate overfitting. Early stopping halts training when validation performance degrades. Dropout randomly disables neurons during training.

question: A company has a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) application that uses a vector database to store embeddings of documents. The company must migrate the application to AWS and must implement a solution that provides semantic search of text files. The company has already migrated the text repository to an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use an AWS Batch job to process the files and generate embeddings. Use AWS Glue to store the embeddings. Use SQL queries to perform the semantic searches.
mcqs.B: Use a custom Amazon SageMaker notebook to run a custom script to generate embeddings. Use SageMaker Feature Store to store the embeddings. Use SQL queries to perform the semantic searches.
mcqs.C: Use the Amazon Kendra S3 connector to ingest the documents from the S3 bucket into Amazon Kendra. Query Amazon Kendra to perform the semantic searches.
mcqs.D: Use an Amazon Textract asynchronous job to ingest the documents from the S3 bucket. Query Amazon Textract to perform the semantic searches.

explanation: Amazon Kendra provides native support for semantic search and can directly ingest documents from S3, making it a suitable choice for this requirement.

question: A company uses Amazon Athena to query a dataset in Amazon S3. The dataset has a target variable that the company wants to predict. The company needs to use the dataset in a solution to determine if a model can predict the target variable. Which solution will provide this information with the LEAST development effort?

mcqs.A: Create a new model by using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Report the model's achieved performance.
mcqs.B: Implement custom scripts to perform data pre-processing, multiple linear regression, and performance evaluation. Run the scripts on Amazon EC2 instances.
mcqs.C: Configure Amazon Macie to analyze the dataset and to create a model. Report the model's achieved performance.
mcqs.D: Select a model from Amazon Bedrock. Tune the model with the data. Report the model's achieved performance.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot automates model development, reducing development effort.

question: A company wants to predict the success of advertising campaigns by considering the color scheme of each advertisement. An ML engineer is preparing data for a neural network model. The dataset includes color information as categorical data. Which technique for feature engineering should the ML engineer use for the model?

mcqs.A: Apply label encoding to the color categories. Automatically assign each color a unique integer.
mcqs.B: Implement padding to ensure that all color feature vectors have the same length.
mcqs.C: Perform dimensionality reduction on the color categories.
mcqs.D: One-hot encode the color categories to transform the color scheme feature into a binary matrix.

explanation: One-hot encoding is suitable for categorical data like color schemes, transforming them into a binary matrix that the neural network can process.

question: A company uses a hybrid cloud environment. A model that is deployed on premises uses data in Amazon S3 to provide customers with a live conversational engine. The model is using sensitive data. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to identify and remove the sensitive data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Deploy the model on Amazon SageMaker. Create a set of AWS Lambda functions to identify and remove the sensitive data.
mcqs.B: Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses AWS Fargate. Create an AWS Batch job to identify and remove the sensitive data.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Macie to identify the sensitive data. Create a set of AWS Lambda functions to remove the sensitive data.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Comprehend to identify the sensitive data. Launch Amazon EC2 instances to remove the sensitive data.

explanation: Amazon Macie can identify sensitive data and Lambda functions can remove it with minimal operational overhead.

question: An ML engineer needs to create data ingestion pipelines and ML model deployment pipelines on AWS. All the raw data is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Data Firehose to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Redshift ML to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use Amazon SageMaker Studio Classic to create the model deployment pipelines.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Athena to create the data ingestion pipelines. Use an Amazon SageMaker notebook to create the model deployment pipelines.

explanation: AWS Glue creates data ingestion pipelines from S3, and SageMaker Studio Classic orchestrates model deployment pipelines.

question: A company that has hundreds of data scientists is using Amazon SageMaker to create ML models. The models are in model groups in the SageMaker Model Registry. The data scientists are grouped into three categories: computer vision, natural language processing (NLP), and speech recognition. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to organize the existing models into these groups to improve model discoverability at scale. The solution must not affect the integrity of the model artifacts and their existing groupings.

mcqs.A: Create a custom tag for each of the three categories. Add the tags to the model packages in the SageMaker Model Registry.
mcqs.B: Create a model group for each category. Move the existing models into these category model groups.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking to automatically identify and tag which model groups should contain the models.
mcqs.D: Create a Model Registry collection for each of the three categories. Move the existing model groups into the collections.

explanation: SageMaker Model Registry collections allow organizing model groups hierarchically, which meets the requirement of organizing models into categories without affecting their integrity.

question: A company runs an Amazon SageMaker domain in a public subnet of a newly created VPC. The network is configured properly, and ML engineers can access the SageMaker domain. Recently, the company discovered suspicious traffic to the domain from a specific IP address. The company needs to block traffic from the specific IP address. Which update to the network configuration will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Create a security group inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the security group to the domain.
mcqs.B: Create a network ACL inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the rule to the default network ACL for the subnet where the domain is located.
mcqs.C: Create a shadow variant for the domain. Configure SageMaker Inference Recommender to send traffic from the specific IP address to the shadow endpoint.
mcqs.D: Create a VPC route table to deny inbound traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the route table to the domain.

explanation: To block traffic from a specific IP address, a network ACL (NACL) is used. Security groups do not support deny rules for inbound traffic; they only allow traffic. Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A company is gathering audio, video, and text data in various languages. The company needs to use a large language model (LLM) to summarize the gathered data that is in Spanish. Which solution will meet these requirements in the LEAST amount of time?

mcqs.A: Train and deploy a model in Amazon SageMaker to convert the data into English text. Train and deploy an LLM in SageMaker to summarize the text.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Jurassic model to summarize the text.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Anthropic Claude model to summarize the text.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Translate to convert the data into English text. Use Amazon Bedrock with the Stable Diffusion model to summarize the text.

explanation: Amazon Transcribe and Translate can quickly convert audio/video to text in Spanish, then Bedrock's Jurassic model can summarize it.

question: A financial company receives a high volume of real-time market data streams from an external provider. The streams consist of thousands of JSON records every second. The company needs to implement a scalable solution on AWS to identify anomalous data points. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Ingest real-time data into Amazon Kinesis data streams. Use the built-in RANDOM_CUT_FOREST function in Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to process the data streams and to detect data anomalies.
mcqs.B: Ingest real-time data into Amazon Kinesis data streams. Deploy an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time outlier detection. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect anomalies. Use the data streams to invoke the Lambda function.
mcqs.C: Ingest real-time data into Apache Kafka on Amazon EC2 instances. Deploy an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time outlier detection. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect anomalies. Use the data streams to invoke the Lambda function.
mcqs.D: Send real-time data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the queue messages. Program the Lambda function to start an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job for batch processing and anomaly detection.

explanation: This solution has the least operational overhead as it utilizes managed services like Amazon Kinesis and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, which can handle real-time data processing and anomaly detection with minimal management.

question: A company has a large collection of chat recordings from customer interactions after a product release. An ML engineer needs to create an ML model to analyze the chat data. The ML engineer needs to determine the success of the product by reviewing customer sentiments about the product. Which action should the ML engineer take to complete the evaluation in the LEAST amount of time?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
mcqs.B: Train a Naive Bayes classifier to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze sentiments of the chat conversations.
mcqs.D: Use random forests to classify sentiments of the chat conversations.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service that can analyze sentiments of text data, making it the fastest option for this task.

question: A company has a conversational AI assistant that sends requests through Amazon Bedrock to an Anthropic Claude large language model (LLM). Users report that when they ask similar questions multiple times, they sometimes receive different answers. An ML engineer needs to improve the responses to be more consistent and less random. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Increase the temperature parameter and the top_k parameter.
mcqs.B: Increase the temperature parameter. Decrease the top_k parameter.
mcqs.C: Decrease the temperature parameter. Increase the top_k parameter.
mcqs.D: Decrease the temperature parameter and the top_k parameter.

explanation: Decreasing the temperature parameter reduces randomness in the model's output, making it more deterministic. Increasing the top_k parameter provides more diverse but still coherent responses; however, decreasing it along with temperature can enhance consistency. This combination helps achieve more consistent and less random responses.

question: A company is using ML to predict the presence of a specific weed in a farmer's field. The company is using the Amazon SageMaker linear learner built-in algorithm with a value of multiclass_classifier for the predictor_type hyperparameter. What should the company do to MINIMIZE false positives?

mcqs.A: Set the value of the weight decay hyperparameter to zero.
mcqs.B: Increase the number of training epochs.
mcqs.C: Increase the value of the target_precision hyperparameter.
mcqs.D: Change the value of the predictor_type hyperparameter to regressor.

explanation: To minimize false positives, the company should increase the target precision, which directly controls the trade-off between precision and recall.

question: A company has implemented a data ingestion pipeline for sales transactions from its ecommerce website. The company uses Amazon Data Firehose to ingest data into Amazon OpenSearch Service. The buffer interval of the Firehose stream is set for 60 seconds. An OpenSearch linear model generates real-time sales forecasts based on the data and presents the data in an OpenSearch dashboard. The company needs to optimize the data ingestion pipeline to support sub-second latency for the real-time dashboard. Which change to the architecture will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use zero buffering in the Firehose stream. Tune the batch size that is used in the PutRecordBatch operation.
mcqs.B: Replace the Firehose stream with an AWS DataSync task. Configure the task with enhanced fan-out consumers.
mcqs.C: Increase the buffer interval of the Firehose stream from 60 seconds to 120 seconds.
mcqs.D: Replace the Firehose stream with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

explanation: Using zero buffering in the Firehose stream allows for immediate delivery of data to OpenSearch Service, reducing latency. Tuning the batch size for PutRecordBatch operation helps optimize performance.

question: A company has trained an ML model in Amazon SageMaker. The company needs to host the model to provide inferences in a production environment. The model must be highly available and must respond with minimum latency. The size of each request will be between 1 KB and 3 MB. The model will receive unpredictable bursts of requests during the day. The inferences must adapt proportionally to the changes in demand. How should the company deploy the model into production to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a SageMaker real-time inference endpoint. Configure auto scaling. Configure the endpoint to present the existing model.
mcqs.B: Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use ECS scheduled scaling that is based on the CPU of the ECS cluster.
mcqs.C: Install SageMaker Operator on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Deploy the model in Amazon EKS. Set horizontal pod auto scaling to scale replicas based on the memory metric.
mcqs.D: Use Spot Instances with a Spot Fleet behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for inferences. Use the ALBRequestCountPerTarget metric as the metric for auto scaling.

explanation: SageMaker real-time endpoints provide synchronous, low-latency inference. Pairing with auto scaling ensures the endpoint adapts to fluctuating traffic demands.

question: An ML engineer needs to use an Amazon EMR cluster to process large volumes of data in batches. Any data loss is unacceptable. Which instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

mcqs.A: Run the primary node, core nodes, and task nodes on On-Demand Instances.
mcqs.B: Run the primary node, core nodes, and task nodes on Spot Instances.
mcqs.C: Run the primary node on an On-Demand Instance. Run the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
mcqs.D: Run the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances. Run the task nodes on Spot Instances.

explanation: Using On-Demand Instances for primary and core nodes ensures reliability, while Spot Instances for task nodes provide cost-effectiveness.

question: A company wants to improve the sustainability of its ML operations. Which actions will reduce the energy usage and computational resources that are associated with the company's training jobs?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to stop training jobs when non-converging conditions are detected.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth for data labeling.
mcqs.C: Deploy models by using AWS Lambda functions.
mcqs.D: Use AWS Trainium instances for training.

explanation: Using Amazon SageMaker Debugger and AWS Trainium instances can reduce energy usage and computational resources.

question: A company is planning to create several ML prediction models. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. The entire dataset is more than 5 TB in size and consists of CSV, JSON, Apache Parquet, and simple text files. The data must be processed in several consecutive steps. The steps include complex manipulations that can take hours to finish running. Some of the processing involves natural language processing (NLP) transformations. The entire process must be automated. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Process data at each step by using Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. Automate the process by using Data Wrangler jobs.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker notebooks for each data processing step. Automate the process by using Amazon EventBridge.
mcqs.C: Process data at each step by using AWS Lambda functions. Automate the process by using AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to create a pipeline of data processing steps. Automate the pipeline by using Amazon EventBridge.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is a fully managed service for building, automating, and managing end-to-end machine learning workflows. It supports complex data processing steps and automation.

question: An ML engineer needs to use AWS CloudFormation to create an ML model that an Amazon SageMaker endpoint will host. Which resource should the ML engineer declare in the CloudFormation template to meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: AWS::SageMaker::Model
mcqs.B: AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint
mcqs.C: AWS::SageMaker::NotebookInstance
mcqs.D: AWS::SageMaker::Pipeline

explanation: The AWS::SageMaker::Model resource creates a model in SageMaker that can be used by an endpoint. This resource is necessary for hosting an ML model on a SageMaker endpoint.

question: An advertising company uses AWS Lake Formation to manage a data lake. The data lake contains structured data and unstructured data. The company's ML engineers are assigned to specific advertisement campaigns. The ML engineers must interact with the data through Amazon Athena and by browsing the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. The ML engineers must have access to only the resources that are specific to their assigned advertisement campaigns. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

mcqs.A: Configure IAM policies on an AWS Glue Data Catalog to restrict access to Athena based on the ML engineers' campaigns.
mcqs.B: Store users and campaign information in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update S3 bucket policies.
mcqs.C: Use Lake Formation to authorize AWS Glue to access the S3 bucket. Configure Lake Formation tags to map ML engineers to their campaigns.
mcqs.D: Configure S3 bucket policies to restrict access to the S3 bucket based on the ML engineers' campaigns.

explanation: Lake Formation tags enable fine-grained access control. This approach allows for efficient management of access based on ML engineers' campaigns.

question: An ML engineer needs to use data with Amazon SageMaker Canvas to train an ML model. The data is stored in Amazon S3 and is complex in structure. The ML engineer must use a file format that minimizes processing time for the data. Which file format will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: CSV files compressed with Snappy
mcqs.B: JSON objects in JSONL format
mcqs.C: JSON files compressed with gzip
mcqs.D: Apache Parquet files

explanation: Apache Parquet files are optimized for complex data structures and provide efficient processing times, making them suitable for minimizing processing time in Amazon SageMaker Canvas.

question: An ML engineer is evaluating several ML models and must choose one model to use in production. The cost of false negative predictions by the models is much higher than the cost of false positive predictions. Which metric finding should the ML engineer prioritize the MOST when choosing the model?

mcqs.A: Low precision
mcqs.B: High precision
mcqs.C: Low recall
mcqs.D: High recall

explanation: The engineer should prioritize high recall because it minimizes false negatives, which have a higher cost. High recall ensures that most actual positive cases are correctly identified.

question: A company has trained and deployed an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker. The company needs to implement a solution to record and monitor all the API call events for the SageMaker endpoint. The solution also must provide a notification when the number of API call events breaches a threshold. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Debugger to track the inferences and to report metrics. Create a custom rule to provide a notification when the threshold is breached.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Debugger to track the inferences and to report metrics. Use the tensor_variance built-in rule to provide a notification when the threshold is breached.
mcqs.C: Log all the endpoint invocation API events by using AWS CloudTrail. Use an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring. Set up a CloudWatch alarm to provide notification when the threshold is breached.
mcqs.D: Add the Invocations metric to an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for monitoring. Set up a CloudWatch alarm to provide notification when the threshold is breached.

explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls, and CloudWatch monitors and alarms can be set up for notifications.

question: A company has AWS Glue data processing jobs that are orchestrated by an AWS Glue workflow. The AWS Glue jobs can run on a schedule or can be launched manually. The company is developing pipelines in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines for ML model development. The pipelines will use the output of the AWS Glue jobs during the data processing phase of model development. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution that integrates the AWS Glue jobs with the pipelines. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use AWS Step Functions for orchestration of the pipelines and the AWS Glue jobs.
mcqs.B: Use processing steps in SageMaker Pipelines. Configure inputs that point to the Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of the AWS Glue jobs.
mcqs.C: Use Callback steps in SageMaker Pipelines to start the AWS Glue workflow and to stop the pipelines until the AWS Glue jobs finish running.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the pipelines and the AWS Glue jobs in the desired order.

explanation: Callback steps in SageMaker Pipelines allow for asynchronous execution and waiting for jobs to complete, making it suitable for integrating with AWS Glue jobs.

question: A company is using an Amazon Redshift database as its single data source. Some of the data is sensitive. A data scientist needs to use some of the sensitive data from the database. An ML engineer must give the data scientist access to the data without transforming the source data and without storing anonymized data in the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

mcqs.A: Configure dynamic data masking policies to control how sensitive data is shared with the data scientist at query time.
mcqs.B: Create a materialized view with masking logic on top of the database. Grant the necessary read permissions to the data scientist.
mcqs.C: Unload the Amazon Redshift data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create schema-on-read with masking logic. Share the view with the data scientist.
mcqs.D: Unload the Amazon Redshift data to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue job to anonymize the data. Share the dataset with the data scientist.

explanation: Dynamic data masking in Amazon Redshift allows for column-level masking based on user roles, making it a straightforward solution for controlling access to sensitive data without altering the source or storing anonymized data.

question: An ML engineer is using a training job to fine-tune a deep learning model in Amazon SageMaker Studio. The ML engineer previously used the same pre-trained model with a similar dataset. The ML engineer expects vanishing gradient, underutilized GPU, and overfitting problems. The ML engineer needs to implement a solution to detect these issues and to react in predefined ways when the issues occur. The solution also must provide comprehensive real-time metrics during the training. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use TensorBoard to monitor the training job. Publish the findings to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the findings and to initiate the predefined actions.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch default metrics to gain insights about the training job. Use the metrics to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the predefined actions.
mcqs.C: Expand the metrics in Amazon CloudWatch to include the gradients in each training step. Use the metrics to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the predefined actions.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Debugger built-in rules to monitor the training job. Configure the rules to initiate the predefined actions.

explanation: SageMaker Debugger provides built-in rules for detecting issues like vanishing gradients and overfitting, and can trigger predefined actions.

question: A credit card company has a fraud detection model in production on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The company develops a new version of the model. The company needs to assess the new model's performance by using live data and without affecting production end users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Set up SageMaker Debugger and create a custom rule.
mcqs.B: Set up blue/green deployments with all-at-once traffic shifting.
mcqs.C: Set up blue/green deployments with canary traffic shifting.
mcqs.D: Set up shadow testing with a shadow variant of the new model.

explanation: Shadow testing allows evaluating a new model with live data without affecting production users. It creates a duplicate of the production variant, sending all traffic to both variants but only using production variant responses.

question: A company stores time-series data about user clicks in an Amazon S3 bucket. The raw data consists of millions of rows of user activity every day. ML engineers access the data to develop their ML models. The ML engineers need to generate daily reports and analyze click trends over the past 3 days by using Amazon Athena. The company must retain the data for 30 days before archiving the data. Which solution will provide the HIGHEST performance for data retrieval?

mcqs.A: Keep all the time-series data without partitioning in the S3 bucket. Manually move data that is older than 30 days to separate S3 buckets.
mcqs.B: Create AWS Lambda functions to copy the time-series data into separate S3 buckets. Apply S3 Lifecycle policies to archive data that is older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
mcqs.C: Organize the time-series data into partitions by date prefix in the S3 bucket. Apply S3 Lifecycle policies to archive partitions that are older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
mcqs.D: Put each day's time-series data into its own S3 bucket. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to archive S3 buckets that hold data that is older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

explanation: Partitioning data by date prefix in S3 enables efficient querying and retrieval of data using Amazon Athena, resulting in the highest performance for data retrieval.

question: A company has deployed an ML model that detects fraudulent credit card transactions in real time in a banking application. The model uses Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference. Consumers are reporting delays in receiving the inference results. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to improve the inference performance. The solution also must provide a notification when a deviation in model quality occurs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker real-time inference for inference. Use SageMaker Model Monitor for notifications about model quality.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker batch transform for inference. Use SageMaker Model Monitor for notifications about model quality.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Serverless Inference for inference. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for notifications about model quality.
mcqs.D: Keep using SageMaker Asynchronous Inference for inference. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for notifications about model quality.

explanation: SageMaker real-time inference provides low latency, improving performance. SageMaker Model Monitor enables automated detection of data and model quality drift, providing notifications.

question: An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to host a trained ML model. The rate of requests to the model will be inconsistent throughout the day. The ML engineer needs a scalable solution that minimizes costs when the model is not in use. The solution also must maintain the model's capacity to respond to requests during times of peak usage. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create AWS Lambda functions that have fixed concurrency to host the model. Configure the Lambda functions to automatically scale based on the number of requests to the model.
mcqs.B: Deploy the model on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses AWS Fargate. Set a static number of tasks to handle requests during times of peak usage.
mcqs.C: Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. Deploy multiple copies of the model to the endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer to route traffic between the different copies of the model at the endpoint.
mcqs.D: Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. Create SageMaker endpoint auto scaling policies that are based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics to adjust the number of instances dynamically.

explanation: SageMaker endpoint auto-scaling allows for dynamic adjustment of instances based on demand, making it suitable for inconsistent request patterns. This approach minimizes costs when idle and maintains capacity during peak usage.

question: A company uses Amazon SageMaker Studio to develop an ML model. The company has a single SageMaker Studio domain. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution that provides an automated alert when SageMaker compute costs reach a specific threshold. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Add resource tagging by editing the SageMaker user profile in the SageMaker domain. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
mcqs.B: Add resource tagging by editing the SageMaker user profile in the SageMaker domain. Configure AWS Budgets to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
mcqs.C: Add resource tagging by editing each user's IAM profile. Configure AWS Cost Explorer to send an alert when the threshold is reached.
mcqs.D: Add resource tagging by editing each user's IAM profile. Configure AWS Budgets to send an alert when the threshold is reached.

explanation: The correct solution involves using AWS Budgets for cost threshold alerts. Tagging resources via the SageMaker domain user profile allows for accurate cost tracking.

question: A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML workloads. The company's ML engineer receives a 50 MB Apache Parquet data file to build a fraud detection model. The file includes several correlated columns that are not required. What should the ML engineer do to drop the unnecessary columns in the file with the LEAST effort?

mcqs.A: Download the file to a local workstation. Perform one-hot encoding by using a custom Python script.
mcqs.B: Create an Apache Spark job that uses a custom processing script on Amazon EMR.
mcqs.C: Create a SageMaker processing job by calling the SageMaker Python SDK.
mcqs.D: Create a data flow in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Configure a transform step.

explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler provides a visual interface to transform and prepare data for ML, making it efficient for dropping unnecessary columns.

question: A company is creating an application that will recommend products for customers to purchase. The application will make API calls to Amazon Q Business. The company must ensure that responses from Amazon Q Business do not include the name of the company's main competitor. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Configure the competitor's name as a blocked phrase in Amazon Q Business.
mcqs.B: Configure an Amazon Q Business retriever to exclude the competitor's name.
mcqs.C: Configure an Amazon Kendra retriever for Amazon Q Business to build indexes that exclude the competitor's name.
mcqs.D: Configure document attribute boosting in Amazon Q Business to deprioritize the competitor's name.

explanation: Configuring the competitor's name as a blocked phrase in Amazon Q Business directly addresses the requirement to exclude the competitor's name from responses.

question: An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker to fine-tune a large language model (LLM) for text summarization. The ML engineer must follow a low-code no-code (LCNC) approach. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Studio to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed by a custom API endpoint.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune an LLM that is deployed by SageMaker JumpStart.

explanation: SageMaker JumpStart provides pre-trained models with built-in fine-tuning workflows. Autopilot enables LCNC fine-tuning of LLMs.

question: A company has an ML model that needs to run one time each night to predict stock values. The model input is 3 MB of data that is collected during the current day. The model produces the predictions for the next day. The prediction process takes less than 1 minute to finish running. How should the company deploy the model on Amazon SageMaker to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use a multi-model serverless endpoint. Enable caching.
mcqs.B: Use an asynchronous inference endpoint. Set the InitialInstanceCount parameter to 0.
mcqs.C: Use a real-time endpoint. Configure an auto scaling policy to scale the model to 0 when the model is not in use.
mcqs.D: Use a serverless inference endpoint. Set the MaxConcurrency parameter to 1.

explanation: SageMaker serverless endpoints auto-scale to zero between invocations, ideal for infrequent workloads like this one.

question: An ML engineer trained an ML model on Amazon SageMaker to detect automobile accidents from closed-circuit TV footage. The ML engineer used SageMaker Data Wrangler to create a training dataset of images of accidents and non-accidents. The model performed well during training and validation. However, the model is underperforming in production because of variations in the quality of the images from various cameras. Which solution will improve the model's accuracy in the LEAST amount of time?

mcqs.A: Collect more images from all the cameras. Use Data Wrangler to prepare a new training dataset.
mcqs.B: Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler corrupt image transform. Specify the impulse noise option.
mcqs.C: Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler enhance image contrast transform. Specify the Gamma contrast option.
mcqs.D: Recreate the training dataset by using the Data Wrangler resize image transform. Crop all images to the same size.

explanation: The model's underperformance is due to variations in image quality. Using Data Wrangler's corrupt image transform with impulse noise can simulate real-world noise, making the model more robust.

question: A company has an application that uses different APIs to generate embeddings for input text. The company needs to implement a solution to automatically rotate the API tokens every 3 months. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Store the tokens in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the rotation.
mcqs.B: Store the tokens in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the rotation.
mcqs.C: Store the tokens in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use an AWS managed key to perform the rotation.
mcqs.D: Store the tokens in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use an AWS owned key to perform the rotation.

explanation: AWS Secrets Manager provides secure storage and automatic rotation of secrets, making it suitable for managing API tokens. This solution allows for the tokens to be rotated every 3 months.

question: An ML engineer receives datasets that contain missing values, duplicates, and extreme outliers. The ML engineer must consolidate these datasets into a single data frame and must prepare the data for ML. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to import the datasets and to consolidate them into a single data frame. Use the cleansing and enrichment functionalities to prepare the data.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to import the datasets and to consolidate them into a single data frame. Use the human-in-the-loop capability to prepare the data.
mcqs.C: Manually import and merge the datasets. Consolidate the datasets into a single data frame. Use Amazon Q Developer to generate code snippets that will prepare the data.
mcqs.D: Manually import and merge the datasets. Consolidate the datasets into a single data frame. Use Amazon SageMaker data labeling to prepare the data.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler is a suitable tool for data preparation, offering data cleansing and enrichment functionalities to handle missing values, duplicates, and outliers.

question: A company has historical data that shows whether customers needed long-term support from company staff. The company needs to develop an ML model to predict whether new customers will require long-term support. Which modeling approach should the company use to meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Anomaly detection
mcqs.B: Linear regression
mcqs.C: Logistic regression
mcqs.D: Semantic segmentation

explanation: This is a binary classification problem, and logistic regression is a suitable approach for predicting probabilities of a binary outcome. It models the probability of an event occurring using a logistic function.

question: An ML engineer has developed a binary classification model outside of Amazon SageMaker. The ML engineer needs to make the model accessible to a SageMaker Canvas user for additional tuning. The model artifacts are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The ML engineer and the Canvas user are part of the same SageMaker domain. Which combination of requirements must be met so that the ML engineer can share the model with the Canvas user?

mcqs.A: The ML engineer and the Canvas user must be in separate SageMaker domains.
mcqs.B: The Canvas user must have permissions to access the S3 bucket where the model artifacts are stored.
mcqs.C: The model must be registered in the SageMaker Model Registry.
mcqs.D: The ML engineer must host the model on AWS Marketplace.

explanation: The model must be registered in SageMaker Model Registry and the Canvas user must have access to the S3 bucket.
