question: A company is building a deep learning model on Amazon SageMaker. The company uses a large amount of data as the training dataset. The company needs to optimize the model's hyperparameters to minimize the loss function on the validation dataset. Which hyperparameter tuning strategy will accomplish this goal with the LEAST computation time?

mcqs.A: Hyperband
mcqs.B: Grid search
mcqs.C: Bayesian optimization
mcqs.D: Random search

explanation: Hyperband is a strategy that optimizes hyperparameters with the least computation time by focusing on the most promising hyperparameter combinations.

question: A company is planning to use Amazon Redshift ML in its primary AWS account. The source data is in an Amazon S3 bucket in a secondary account. An ML engineer needs to set up an ML pipeline in the primary account to access the S3 bucket in the secondary account. The solution must not require public IPv4 addresses. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC with no public access enabled in the primary account. Create a VPC peering connection between the accounts. Update the VPC route tables to remove the route to 0.0.0.0/0.
mcqs.B: Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC with no public access enabled in the primary account. Create an AWS Direct Connect connection and a transit gateway. Associate the VPCs from both accounts with the transit gateway. Update the VPC route tables to remove the route to 0.0.0.0/0.
mcqs.C: Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC in the primary account. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with two encrypted IPsec tunnels between the accounts. Set up interface VPC endpoints for Amazon S3.
mcqs.D: Provision a Redshift cluster and Amazon SageMaker Studio in a VPC in the primary account. Create an S3 gateway endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow IAM principals from the primary account. Set up interface VPC endpoints for SageMaker and Amazon Redshift.

explanation: This solution allows access to S3 without requiring public IPv4 addresses. Using an S3 gateway endpoint and updating the S3 bucket policy enables secure cross-account access.

question: A company is using an AWS Lambda function to monitor the metrics from an ML model. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to send an email message when the metrics breach a threshold. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Log the metrics from the Lambda function to AWS CloudTrail. Configure a CloudTrail trail to send the email message.
mcqs.B: Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudFront. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send the email message.
mcqs.C: Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudWatch. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to send the email message.
mcqs.D: Log the metrics from the Lambda function to Amazon CloudWatch. Configure an Amazon CloudFront rule to send the email message.

explanation: Logging metrics to CloudWatch and configuring a CloudWatch alarm is a standard approach for monitoring and alerting on metric thresholds. CloudWatch alarms can directly trigger actions like sending SNS notifications, which can be used to send email messages.

question: A company has used Amazon SageMaker to deploy a predictive ML model in production. The company is using SageMaker Model Monitor on the model. After a model update, an ML engineer notices data quality issues in the Model Monitor checks. What should the ML engineer do to mitigate the data quality issues that Model Monitor has identified?

mcqs.A: Adjust the model's parameters and hyperparameters.
mcqs.B: Initiate a manual Model Monitor job that uses the most recent production data.
mcqs.C: Create a new baseline from the latest dataset. Update Model Monitor to use the new baseline for evaluations.
mcqs.D: Include additional data in the existing training set for the model. Retrain and redeploy the model.

explanation: The engineer should create a new baseline from the latest dataset and update Model Monitor to use the new baseline for evaluations. This allows Model Monitor to assess data quality based on the updated data distribution. This approach directly addresses the data quality issues identified.

question: A company has an ML model that generates text descriptions based on images that customers upload to the company's website. The images can be up to 50 MB in total size. An ML engineer decides to store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. The ML engineer must implement a processing solution that can scale to accommodate changes in demand. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job to process all the images in the S3 bucket.
mcqs.B: Create an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint and a scaling policy. Run a script to make an inference request for each image.
mcqs.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Karpenter for auto scaling. Host the model on the EKS cluster. Run a script to make an inference request for each image.
mcqs.D: Create an AWS Batch job that uses an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Specify a list of images to process for each AWS Batch job.

explanation: SageMaker asynchronous inference handles large payloads and long processing times with auto scaling.

question: An ML engineer needs to use AWS services to identify and extract meaningful unique keywords from documents. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) library on Amazon EC2 instances for text pre-processing. Use the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm to identify and extract relevant keywords.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker and the BlazingText algorithm. Apply custom pre-processing steps for stemming and removal of stop words. Calculate term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) scores to identify and extract relevant keywords.
mcqs.C: Store the documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create AWS Lambda functions to process the documents and to run Python scripts for stemming and removal of stop words. Use bigram and trigram techniques to identify and extract relevant keywords.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognition and key phrase extraction to identify and extract relevant keywords.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides a managed service for key phrase extraction, reducing operational overhead. This approach eliminates the need for custom code and infrastructure management. It directly supports the requirement to identify and extract meaningful keywords.

question: A company needs to give its ML engineers appropriate access to training data. The ML engineers must access training data from only their own business group. The ML engineers must not be allowed to access training data from other business groups. The company uses a single AWS account and stores all the training data in Amazon S3 buckets. All ML model training occurs in Amazon SageMaker. Which solution will provide the ML engineers with the appropriate access?

mcqs.A: Enable S3 bucket versioning.
mcqs.B: Configure S3 Object Lock settings for each user.
mcqs.C: Add cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) policies to the S3 buckets.
mcqs.D: Create IAM policies. Attach the policies to IAM users or IAM roles.

explanation: Using IAM policies allows for fine-grained access control, enabling ML engineers to access only their own business group's data. This approach ensures that ML engineers cannot access data from other business groups.

question: A company needs to host a custom ML model to perform forecast analysis. The forecast analysis will occur with predictable and sustained load during the same 2-hour period every day. Multiple invocations during the analysis period will require quick responses. The company needs AWS to manage the underlying infrastructure and any auto scaling activities. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Schedule an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job by using AWS Lambda.
mcqs.B: Configure an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to use scheduled scaling.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference with provisioned concurrency.
mcqs.D: Run the model on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2 with pod auto scaling.

explanation: SageMaker Serverless Inference with provisioned concurrency provides auto-scaling and manages underlying infrastructure, meeting the requirements for predictable load and quick responses.

question: A company's ML engineer has deployed an ML model for sentiment analysis to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The ML engineer needs to explain to company stakeholders how the model makes predictions. Which solution will provide an explanation for the model's predictions?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Model Monitor on the deployed model.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Clarify on the deployed model.
mcqs.C: Show the distribution of inferences from A/B testing in Amazon CloudWatch.
mcqs.D: Add a shadow endpoint. Analyze prediction differences on samples.

explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides real-time SHAP feature attributions for each inference request, helping explain individual predictions.

question: An ML engineer is using Amazon SageMaker to train a deep learning model that requires distributed training. After some training attempts, the ML engineer observes that the instances are not performing as expected. The ML engineer identifies communication overhead between the training instances. What should the ML engineer do to MINIMIZE the communication overhead between the instances?

mcqs.A: Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in a different AWS Region from where the instances are deployed.
mcqs.B: Place the instances in the same VPC subnet but in different Availability Zones. Store the data in a different AWS Region from where the instances are deployed.
mcqs.C: Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in the same AWS Region and Availability Zone where the instances are deployed.
mcqs.D: Place the instances in the same VPC subnet. Store the data in the same AWS Region but in a different Availability Zone from where the instances are deployed.

explanation: To minimize communication overhead, instances should be in the same VPC subnet and data should be in the same AWS Region and Availability Zone to reduce latency and data transfer times.

question: A company is running ML models on premises by using custom Python scripts and proprietary datasets. The company is using PyTorch. The model building requires unique domain knowledge. The company needs to move the models to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker built-in algorithms to train the proprietary datasets.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker script mode and premade images for ML frameworks.
mcqs.C: Build a container on AWS that includes custom packages and a choice of ML frameworks.
mcqs.D: Purchase similar production models through AWS Marketplace.

explanation: SageMaker script mode allows custom Python scripts with popular frameworks like PyTorch. This approach requires the least effort as it supports existing scripts and frameworks.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker and millions of files to train an ML model. Each file is several megabytes in size. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to improve training performance. Which solution will meet these requirements in the LEAST amount of time?

mcqs.A: Transfer the data to a new S3 bucket that provides S3 Express One Zone storage. Adjust the training job to use the new S3 bucket.
mcqs.B: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Link the file system to the existing S3 bucket. Adjust the training job to read from the file system.
mcqs.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Transfer the existing data to the file system. Adjust the training job to read from the file system.
mcqs.D: Create an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) cluster. Link the Redis OSS cluster to the existing S3 bucket. Stream the data from the Redis OSS cluster directly to the training job.

explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre provides high-throughput, low-latency parallel file system access, directly integrating with S3, ideal for training jobs that need fast reads of millions of small files.

question: A company wants to develop an ML model by using tabular data from its customers. The data contains meaningful ordered features with sensitive information that should not be discarded. An ML engineer must ensure that the sensitive data is masked before another team starts to build the model. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Macie to categorize the sensitive data.
mcqs.B: Prepare the data by using AWS Glue DataBrew.
mcqs.C: Run an AWS Batch job to change the sensitive data to random values.
mcqs.D: Run an Amazon EMR job to change the sensitive data to random values.

explanation: AWS Glue DataBrew can be used to prepare and mask sensitive data. It provides data transformation and data quality capabilities.

question: An ML engineer needs to deploy ML models to get inferences from large datasets in an asynchronous manner. The ML engineer also needs to implement scheduled monitoring of the data quality of the models. The ML engineer must receive alerts when changes in data quality occur. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Deploy the models by using scheduled AWS Glue jobs. Use Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
mcqs.B: Deploy the models by using scheduled AWS Batch jobs. Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
mcqs.C: Deploy the models by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. Use Amazon EventBridge to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.
mcqs.D: Deploy the models by using Amazon SageMaker batch transform. Use SageMaker Model Monitor to monitor the data quality and to send alerts.

explanation: SageMaker Batch Transform enables asynchronous inference on large datasets. SageMaker Model Monitor provides scheduled monitoring of data quality and alerting.

question: An ML engineer normalized training data by using min-max normalization in AWS Glue DataBrew. The ML engineer must normalize the production inference data in the same way as the training data before passing the production inference data to the model for predictions. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Apply statistics from a well-known dataset to normalize the production samples.
mcqs.B: Keep the min-max normalization statistics from the training set. Use these values to normalize the production samples.
mcqs.C: Calculate a new set of min-max normalization statistics from a batch of production samples. Use these values to normalize all the production samples.
mcqs.D: Calculate a new set of min-max normalization statistics from each production sample. Use these values to normalize all the production samples.

explanation: To ensure consistency, the same normalization statistics used for training must be applied to production data. Keeping the min-max normalization statistics from the training set and using these values to normalize the production samples meets this requirement.

question: A company is planning to use Amazon SageMaker to make classification ratings that are based on images. The company has 6 TB of training data that is stored on an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP system virtual machine (SVM). The SVM is in the same VPC as SageMaker. An ML engineer must make the training data accessible for ML models that are in the SageMaker environment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Mount the FSx for ONTAP file system as a volume to the SageMaker Instance.
mcqs.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to link the S3 bucket to the FSx for ONTAP file system.
mcqs.C: Create a catalog connection from SageMaker Data Wrangler to the FSx for ONTAP file system.
mcqs.D: Create a direct connection from SageMaker Data Wrangler to the FSx for ONTAP file system.

explanation: Mounting the FSx for ONTAP file system directly to the SageMaker instance allows for efficient access to the large training dataset. This approach bypasses the need for data movement or complex setup. It enables seamless integration with the SageMaker environment.

question: A company regularly receives new training data from the vendor of an ML model. The vendor delivers cleaned and prepared data to the company's Amazon S3 bucket every 3-4 days. The company has an Amazon SageMaker pipeline to retrain the model. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to run the pipeline when new data is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

mcqs.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transfer the data to the SageMaker training instance and to initiate training.
mcqs.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to initiate the pipeline when new data is uploaded.
mcqs.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has an event pattern that matches the S3 upload. Configure the pipeline as the target of the rule.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) to orchestrate the pipeline when new data is uploaded.

explanation: Amazon EventBridge can trigger the SageMaker pipeline directly when new data is uploaded to S3, requiring minimal operational effort.

question: An ML engineer is developing a fraud detection model by using the Amazon SageMaker XGBoost algorithm. The model classifies transactions as either fraudulent or legitimate. During testing, the model excels at identifying fraud in the training dataset. However, the model is inefficient at identifying fraud in new and unseen transactions. What should the ML engineer do to improve the fraud detection for new transactions?

mcqs.A: Increase the learning rate.
mcqs.B: Remove some irrelevant features from the training dataset.
mcqs.C: Increase the value of the max_depth hyperparameter.
mcqs.D: Decrease the value of the max_depth hyperparameter.

explanation: The model overfits the training data, indicated by its poor performance on new transactions. Decreasing max_depth reduces model complexity, which can help prevent overfitting. This allows the model to generalize better to unseen data.

question: A company has a binary classification model in production. An ML engineer needs to develop a new version of the model. The new model version must maximize correct predictions of positive labels and negative labels. The ML engineer must use a metric to recalibrate the model to meet these requirements. Which metric should the ML engineer use for the model recalibration?

mcqs.A: Accuracy
mcqs.B: Precision
mcqs.C: Recall
mcqs.D: Specificity

explanation: Accuracy measures the proportion of correct predictions out of all predictions made, making it suitable for maximizing correct predictions of both positive and negative labels.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker to create ML models. The company's data scientists need fine-grained control of the ML workflows that they orchestrate. The data scientists also need the ability to visualize SageMaker jobs and workflows as a directed acyclic graph (DAG). The data scientists must keep a running history of model discovery experiments and must establish model governance for auditing and compliance verifications. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use AWS CodePipeline and its integration with SageMaker Studio to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.
mcqs.B: Use AWS CodePipeline and its integration with SageMaker Experiments to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker Experiments for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Pipelines and its integration with SageMaker Studio to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Pipelines and its integration with SageMaker Experiments to manage the entire ML workflows. Use SageMaker Experiments for the running history of experiments and for auditing and compliance verifications.

explanation: SageMaker Pipelines provides native ML workflow orchestration with DAG visualization. It integrates with SageMaker Studio for fine-grained control and with SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking for experiment history and governance.

question: A company wants to reduce the cost of its containerized ML applications. The applications use ML models that run on Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The EC2 workloads and ECS workloads use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to save predictions and artifacts. An ML engineer must identify resources that are being used inefficiently. The ML engineer also must generate recommendations to reduce the cost of these resources. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

mcqs.A: Create code to evaluate each instance's memory and compute usage.
mcqs.B: Add cost allocation tags to the resources. Activate the tags in AWS Billing and Cost Management.
mcqs.C: Check AWS CloudTrail event history for the creation of the resources.
mcqs.D: Run AWS Compute Optimizer.

explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer provides recommendations to optimize resource utilization and reduce costs.

question: A company needs to create a central catalog for all the company's ML models. The models are in AWS accounts where the company developed the models initially. The models are hosted in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Configure ECR cross-account replication for each existing ECR repository. Ensure that each model is visible in each AWS account.
mcqs.B: Create a new AWS account with a new ECR repository as the central catalog. Configure ECR cross-account replication between the initial ECR repositories and the central catalog.
mcqs.C: Use the Amazon SageMaker Model Registry to create a model group for models hosted in Amazon ECR. Create a new AWS account. In the new account, use the SageMaker Model Registry as the central catalog. Attach a cross-account resource policy to each model group in the initial AWS accounts.
mcqs.D: Use an AWS Glue Data Catalog to store the models. Run an AWS Glue crawler to migrate the models from the ECR repositories to the Data Catalog. Configure cross-account access to the Data Catalog.

explanation: SageMaker Model Registry provides a unified model catalog. Cross-account resource policies enable access to models across accounts. This approach avoids duplicating container images.

question: A company has developed a new ML model. The company requires online model validation on 10% of the traffic before the company fully releases the model in production. The company uses an Amazon SageMaker endpoint behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to serve the model. Which solution will set up the required online validation with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use production variants to add the new model to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Set the variant weight to 0.1 for the new model. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
mcqs.B: Use production variants to add the new model to the existing SageMaker endpoint. Set the variant weight to 1 for the new model. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
mcqs.C: Create a new SageMaker endpoint. Use production variants to add the new model to the new endpoint. Monitor the number of invocations by using Amazon CloudWatch.
mcqs.D: Configure the ALB to route 10% of the traffic to the new model at the existing SageMaker endpoint. Monitor the number of invocations by using AWS CloudTrail.

explanation: Production variants in SageMaker allow A/B testing by allocating a percentage of traffic to a new model. Setting the variant weight to 0.1 enables 10% traffic allocation for validation. This approach has the least operational overhead.

question: A company needs to develop an ML model. The model must identify an item in an image and must provide the location of the item. Which Amazon SageMaker algorithm will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Image classification
mcqs.B: XGBoost
mcqs.C: Object detection
mcqs.D: K-nearest neighbors (k-NN)

explanation: Object Detection algorithm in SageMaker identifies objects in images and returns bounding boxes with class labels and confidence scores, ideal for localization tasks.

question: A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains 1 TB of files from different sources. The S3 bucket contains the following file types in the same S3 folder: CSV, JSON, XLSX, and Apache Parquet. An ML engineer must implement a solution that uses AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. The ML engineer also must store the final output in Amazon S3 so that AWS Glue can consume the output in the future. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use DataBrew to process the existing S3 folder. Store the output in Apache Parquet format.
mcqs.B: Use DataBrew to process the existing S3 folder. Store the output in AWS Glue Parquet format.
mcqs.C: Separate the data into a different folder for each file type. Use DataBrew to process each folder individually. Store the output in Apache Parquet format.
mcqs.D: Separate the data into a different folder for each file type. Use DataBrew to process each folder individually. Store the output in AWS Glue Parquet format.

explanation: DataBrew requires data to be in a single format. Separating data into different folders by file type and processing individually allows for correct output.

question: A manufacturing company uses an ML model to determine whether products meet a standard for quality. The model produces an output of Passed or Failed. Robots separate the products into the two categories by using the model to analyze photos on the assembly line. Which metrics should the company use to evaluate the model's performance?

mcqs.A: Precision and recall
mcqs.B: Root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)
mcqs.C: Accuracy and F1 score
mcqs.D: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score

explanation: Precision, recall, accuracy, and F1 score are suitable for evaluating binary classification models like this one. Precision and recall are particularly useful for imbalanced datasets or when one type of error is more costly than the other.

question: An ML engineer needs to encrypt all data in transit when an ML training job runs. The ML engineer must ensure that encryption in transit is applied to processes that Amazon SageMaker uses during the training job. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Encrypt communication between nodes for batch processing.
mcqs.B: Encrypt communication between nodes in a training cluster.
mcqs.C: Specify an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key during creation of the training job request.
mcqs.D: Specify an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key during creation of the SageMaker domain.

explanation: Enabling inter-container traffic encryption in SageMaker encrypts all node-to-node communication during distributed training with TLS.

question: An ML engineer needs to use metrics to assess the quality of a time-series forecasting model. Which metrics apply to this model?

mcqs.A: Recall
mcqs.B: LogLoss
mcqs.C: Root mean square error (RMSE)
mcqs.D: InferenceLatency

explanation: RMSE and another metric like Average weighted quantile loss (wQL) are suitable for time-series forecasting. RMSE measures the square root of the average of squared errors, suitable for assessing model accuracy.

question: A company runs Amazon SageMaker ML models that use accelerated instances. The models require real-time responses. Each model has different scaling requirements. The company must not allow a cold start for the models. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint for each model. Use provisioned concurrency for the endpoints.
mcqs.B: Create a SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint for each model. Create an auto scaling policy for each endpoint.
mcqs.C: Create a SageMaker endpoint. Create an inference component for each model. In the inference component settings, specify the newly created endpoint. Create an auto scaling policy for each inference component. Set the parameter for the minimum number of copies to at least 1.
mcqs.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Store all the model artifacts in the S3 bucket. Create a SageMaker multi-model endpoint. Point the endpoint to the S3 bucket. Create an auto scaling policy for the endpoint. Set the parameter for the minimum number of copies to at least 1.

explanation: This solution meets requirements as it allows for real-time responses, different scaling requirements for each model, and no cold start. Using inference components with a SageMaker endpoint enables these features.

question: A company uses Amazon SageMaker for its ML process. A compliance audit discovers that an Amazon S3 bucket for training data uses server-side encryption with S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). The company requires customer managed keys. An ML engineer changes the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). After the change to the encryption settings, SageMaker training jobs start to fail with AccessDenied errors. What should the ML engineer do to resolve this problem?

mcqs.A: Update the IAM policy that is attached to the execution role for the training jobs. Include the s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject permissions.
mcqs.B: Update the S3 bucket policy that is attached to the S3 bucket. Set the value of the aws:SecureTransport condition key to True.
mcqs.C: Update the IAM policy that is attached to the execution role for the training jobs. Include the kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt permissions.
mcqs.D: Update the IAM policy that is attached to the user that created the training jobs. Include the kms:CreateGrant permission.

explanation: The ML engineer needs to update the IAM policy to include KMS permissions.

question: A company runs training jobs on Amazon SageMaker by using a compute optimized instance. Demand for training runs will remain constant for the next 55 weeks. The instance needs to run for 35 hours each week. The company needs to reduce its model training costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use a serverless endpoint with a provisioned concurrency of 35 hours for each week. Run the training on the endpoint.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Edge Manager for the training. Specify the instance requirement in the edge device configuration. Run the training.
mcqs.C: Use the heterogeneous cluster feature of SageMaker Training. Configure the instance_type, instance_count, and instance_groups arguments to run training jobs.
mcqs.D: Opt in to a SageMaker Savings Plan with a 1-year term and an All Upfront payment. Run a SageMaker Training job on the instance.

explanation: SageMaker Savings Plans provide up to 64% savings over On-Demand pricing for consistent SageMaker usage.

question: A company deployed an ML model that uses the XGBoost algorithm to predict product failures. The model is hosted on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint and is trained on normal operating data. An AWS Lambda function provides the predictions to the company's application. An ML engineer must implement a solution that uses incoming live data to detect decreased model accuracy over time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to create a dashboard that monitors real-time inference data and model predictions. Use the dashboard to detect drift.
mcqs.B: Modify the Lambda function to calculate model drift by using real-time inference data and model predictions. Program the Lambda function to send alerts.
mcqs.C: Schedule a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Use the job to detect drift by analyzing the live data against a baseline of the training data statistics and constraints.
mcqs.D: Schedule a monitoring job in SageMaker Debugger. Use the job to detect drift by analyzing the live data against a baseline of the training data statistics and constraints.

explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor is used to detect drift by analyzing live data against a baseline of training data statistics and constraints.

question: A company has an ML model that uses historical transaction data to predict customer behavior. An ML engineer is optimizing the model in Amazon SageMaker to enhance the model's predictive accuracy. The ML engineer must examine the input data and the resulting predictions to identify trends that could skew the model's performance across different demographics. Which solution will provide this level of analysis?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor network metrics and CPU metrics for resource optimization during model training.
mcqs.B: Create AWS Glue DataBrew recipes to correct the data based on statistics from the model output.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Clarify to evaluate the model and training data for underlying patterns that might affect accuracy.
mcqs.D: Create AWS Lambda functions to automate data pre-processing and to ensure consistent quality of input data for the model.

explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides model explainability and bias detection, which helps identify trends that could skew the model's performance across different demographics.

question: A company uses 10 Reserved Instances of accelerated instance types to serve the current version of an ML model. An ML engineer needs to deploy a new version of the model to an Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoint. The solution must use the original 10 instances to serve both versions of the model. The solution also must include one additional Reserved Instance that is available to use in the deployment process. The transition between versions must occur with no downtime or service interruptions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Configure a blue/green deployment with all-at-once traffic shifting.
mcqs.B: Configure a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting and a size of 10%.
mcqs.C: Configure a shadow test with a traffic sampling percentage of 10%.
mcqs.D: Configure a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size of 1.

explanation: A rolling deployment with a batch size of 1 allows for updating instances one by one, ensuring no downtime. This approach utilizes the original 10 instances and an additional one for a seamless transition.

question: An IoT company uses Amazon SageMaker to train and test an XGBoost model for object detection. ML engineers need to monitor performance metrics when they train the model with variants in hyperparameters. The ML engineers also need to send Short Message Service (SMS) text messages after training is complete. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for message delivery.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for message delivery.
mcqs.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for message delivery.
mcqs.D: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor performance metrics. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for message delivery.

explanation: Amazon CloudWatch is suitable for monitoring performance metrics, and Amazon SNS can send SMS text messages. This combination meets both requirements.

question: A company is working on an ML project that will include Amazon SageMaker notebook instances. An ML engineer must ensure that the SageMaker notebook instances do not allow root access. Which solution will prevent the deployment of notebook instances that allow root access?

mcqs.A: Use IAM condition keys to stop deployments of SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stop deployments of SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
mcqs.C: Monitor resource creation by using Amazon EventBridge events. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes all deployed SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.
mcqs.D: Monitor resource creation by using AWS CloudFormation events. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes all deployed SageMaker notebook instances that allow root access.

explanation: Using IAM condition keys can enforce the required configuration during the creation of SageMaker notebook instances, preventing those with root access from being deployed.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker to develop ML models. The company stores sensitive training data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The model training must have network isolation from the internet. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Run the SageMaker training jobs in private subnets. Create a NAT gateway. Route traffic for training through the NAT gateway.
mcqs.B: Run the SageMaker training jobs in private subnets. Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint. Route traffic for training through the S3 gateway VPC endpoint.
mcqs.C: Run the SageMaker training jobs in public subnets that have an attached security group. In the security group, use inbound rules to limit traffic from the internet. Encrypt SageMaker instance storage by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
mcqs.D: Encrypt traffic to Amazon S3 by using a bucket policy that includes a value of True for the aws:SecureTransport condition key. Use default at-rest encryption for Amazon S3. Encrypt SageMaker instance storage by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

explanation: Using a VPC endpoint for S3 ensures that data does not traverse the public internet. This setup provides network isolation for SageMaker training jobs.

question: A company needs an AWS solution that will automatically create versions of ML models as the models are created. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)
mcqs.B: Model packages from Amazon SageMaker Marketplace
mcqs.C: Amazon SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking
mcqs.D: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry

explanation: SageMaker Model Registry automatically versions models as model packages within model groups, tracking lineage and metadata.

question: A company needs to use Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to supplement an open source large language model (LLM) that runs on Amazon Bedrock. The company's data for RAG is a set of documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. The documents consist of .csv files and .docx files. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create a pipeline in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to generate a new model. Call the new model from Amazon Bedrock to perform RAG queries.
mcqs.B: Convert the data into vectors. Store the data in an Amazon Neptune database. Connect the database to Amazon Bedrock. Call the Amazon Bedrock API to perform RAG queries.
mcqs.C: Fine-tune an existing LLM by using an AutoML job in Amazon SageMaker. Configure the S3 bucket as a data source for the AutoML job. Deploy the LLM to a SageMaker endpoint. Use the endpoint to perform RAG queries.
mcqs.D: Create a knowledge base for Amazon Bedrock. Configure a data source that references the S3 bucket. Use the Amazon Bedrock API to perform RAG queries.

explanation: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides a fully managed RAG pipeline handling document ingestion, embedding, vector storage, and retrieval automatically.

question: A company plans to deploy an ML model for production inference on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The average inference payload size will vary from 100 MB to 300 MB. Inference requests must be processed in 60 minutes or less. Which SageMaker inference option will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Serverless inference
mcqs.B: Asynchronous inference
mcqs.C: Real-time inference
mcqs.D: Batch transform

explanation: SageMaker asynchronous inference handles large payloads (up to 1 GB) and long processing times (up to 60 min). This makes it suitable for sporadic, large-payload workloads.

question: An ML engineer notices class imbalance in an image classification training job. What should the ML engineer do to resolve this issue?

mcqs.A: Reduce the size of the dataset.
mcqs.B: Transform some of the images in the dataset.
mcqs.C: Apply random oversampling on the dataset.
mcqs.D: Apply random data splitting on the dataset.

explanation: Class imbalance can be addressed by oversampling the minority class. Random oversampling is a technique to balance the classes.

question: A company receives daily .csv files about customer interactions with its ML model. The company stores the files in Amazon S3 and uses the files to retrain the model. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to mask credit card numbers in the files before the model is retrained. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

mcqs.A: Create a discovery job in Amazon Macie. Configure the job to find and mask sensitive data.
mcqs.B: Create Apache Spark code to run on an AWS Glue job. Use the Sensitive Data Detection functionality in AWS Glue to find and mask sensitive data.
mcqs.C: Create Apache Spark code to run on an AWS Glue job. Program the code to perform a regex operation to find and mask sensitive data.
mcqs.D: Create Apache Spark code to run on an Amazon EC2 instance. Program the code to perform an operation to find and mask sensitive data.

explanation: Using AWS Glue's Sensitive Data Detection functionality requires less development effort compared to writing custom code for regex operations or setting up Amazon Macie for this specific task.

question: A medical company is using AWS to build a tool to recommend treatments for patients. The company has obtained health records and self-reported textual information in English from patients. The company needs to use this information to gain insight about the patients. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker to build a recurrent neural network (RNN) to summarize the data.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to summarize the data.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Kendra to create a quick-search tool to query the data.
mcqs.D: Use the Amazon SageMaker Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq) algorithm to create a text summary from the data.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend Medical is a managed service that can extract relevant information from unstructured text, specifically designed for medical data. This approach requires the least development effort compared to building a custom model with SageMaker or using a more general search tool like Kendra.

question: A company needs to extract entities from a PDF document to build a classifier model. Which solution will extract and store the entities in the LEAST amount of time?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Comprehend to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.
mcqs.B: Use an open source AI optical character recognition (OCR) tool on Amazon SageMaker to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Textract to extract the entities. Use Amazon Comprehend to convert the entities to text. Store the output in Amazon S3.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Textract integrated with Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) to extract the entities. Store the output in Amazon S3.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend can directly extract entities from text, making it the fastest option. It can process text from PDFs after it has been extracted by an OCR tool or directly if text is already available.

question: A company shares Amazon SageMaker Studio notebooks that are accessible through a VPN. The company must enforce access controls to prevent malicious actors from exploiting presigned URLs to access the notebooks. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Set up Studio client IP validation by using the aws:sourceIp IAM policy condition.
mcqs.B: Set up Studio client VPC validation by using the aws:sourceVpc IAM policy condition.
mcqs.C: Set up Studio client role endpoint validation by using the aws:PrimaryTag IAM policy condition.
mcqs.D: Set up Studio client user endpoint validation by using the aws:PrincipalTag IAM policy condition.

explanation: Using aws:sourceIp IAM policy condition restricts access to specific IP ranges or VPN CIDRs, preventing unauthorized network access to SageMaker notebooks via presigned URLs.

question: An ML engineer needs to merge and transform data from two sources to retrain an existing ML model. One data source consists of .csv files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each .csv file consists of millions of records. The other data source is an Amazon Aurora DB cluster. The result of the merge process must be written to a second S3 bucket. The ML engineer needs to perform this merge-and-transform task every week. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create a transient Amazon EMR cluster every week. Use the cluster to run an Apache Spark job to merge and transform the data.
mcqs.B: Create a weekly AWS Glue job that uses the Apache Spark engine. Use DynamicFrame native operations to merge and transform the data.
mcqs.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs Apache Spark code every week to merge and transform the data. Configure the Lambda function to connect to the initial S3 bucket and the DB cluster.
mcqs.D: Create an AWS Batch job that runs Apache Spark code on Amazon EC2 instances every week. Configure the Spark code to save the data from the EC2 instances to the second S3 bucket.

explanation: AWS Glue provides a managed ETL service that can handle large-scale data processing with minimal operational overhead.

question: An ML engineer has deployed an Amazon SageMaker model to a serverless endpoint in production. The model is invoked by the InvokeEndpoint API operation. The model's latency in production is higher than the baseline latency in the test environment. The ML engineer thinks that the increase in latency is because of model startup time. What should the ML engineer do to confirm or deny this hypothesis?

mcqs.A: Schedule a SageMaker Model Monitor job. Observe metrics about model quality.
mcqs.B: Schedule a SageMaker Model Monitor job with Amazon CloudWatch metrics enabled.
mcqs.C: Enable Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Observe the ModelSetupTime metric in the SageMaker namespace.
mcqs.D: Enable Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Observe the ModelLoadingWaitTime metric in the SageMaker namespace.

explanation: The ModelSetupTime CloudWatch metric measures cold-start latency for serverless endpoints, which is the time to provision resources and load the model.

question: An ML engineer needs to ensure that a dataset complies with regulations for personally identifiable information (PII). The ML engineer will use the data to train an ML model on Amazon SageMaker instances. SageMaker must not use any of the PII. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

mcqs.A: Use the Amazon Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API call to redact the PII from the data. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Access the S3 bucket from the SageMaker instances for model training.
mcqs.B: Use the Amazon Comprehend DetectPiiEntities API call to redact the PII from the data. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system to the SageMaker instances for model training.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to cleanse the dataset of PII. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system to the SageMaker instances for model training.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Macie for automatic discovery of PII in the data. Remove the PII. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the SageMaker instances for model training.

explanation: Using Amazon Comprehend to redact PII and storing data in S3 is efficient. S3 is a scalable storage solution that can be easily accessed by SageMaker for model training.

question: A company must install a custom script on any newly created Amazon SageMaker notebook instances. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create a lifecycle configuration script to install the custom script when a new SageMaker notebook is created. Attach the lifecycle configuration to every new SageMaker notebook as part of the creation steps.
mcqs.B: Create a custom Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) image that contains the custom script. Push the ECR image to a Docker registry. Attach the Docker image to a SageMaker Studio domain. Select the kernel to run as part of the SageMaker notebook.
mcqs.C: Create a custom package index repository. Use AWS CodeArtifact to manage the installation of the custom script. Set up AWS PrivateLink endpoints to connect CodeArtifact to the SageMaker instance. Install the script.
mcqs.D: Store the custom script in Amazon S3. Create an AWS Lambda function to install the custom script on new SageMaker notebooks. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function when a new SageMaker notebook is initialized.

explanation: SageMaker lifecycle configurations automate installation of scripts on notebook instances at creation or start.

question: A company is building a real-time data processing pipeline for an ecommerce application. The application generates a high volume of clickstream data that must be ingested, processed, and visualized in near real time. The company needs a solution that supports SQL for data processing and Jupyter notebooks for interactive analysis. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Data Firehose to ingest the data. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the data. Store the processed data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Use Amazon Data Firehose to transform the data. Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to ingest the data. Use AWS Glue with PySpark to process the data. Store the processed data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to ingest the data. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to process the data. Use the built-in Flink dashboard to visualize the data.

explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink supports SQL and Jupyter-style interactive analysis on streaming data, ideal for real-time clickstream analytics.

question: A medical company needs to store clinical data. The data includes personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information (PHI). An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to ensure that the PII and PHI are not used to train ML models. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Store the clinical data in Amazon S3 buckets. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to mask the PII and PHI before the data is used for model training.
mcqs.B: Upload the clinical data to an Amazon Redshift database. Use built-in SQL stored procedures to automatically classify and mask the PII and PHI before the data is used for model training.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect and mask the PII before the data is used for model training. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and mask the PHI before the data is used for model training.
mcqs.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the PII and PHI. Program the Lambda function to save the encrypted data to an Amazon S3 bucket for model training.

explanation: Amazon Comprehend and Comprehend Medical can detect and mask PII and PHI respectively, making it suitable for protecting sensitive information in ML model training.

question: An ML engineer is developing a classification model. The ML engineer needs to use custom libraries in processing jobs, training jobs, and pipelines in Amazon SageMaker. Which solution will provide this functionality with the LEAST implementation effort?

mcqs.A: Manually install the libraries in the SageMaker containers.
mcqs.B: Build a custom Docker container that includes the required libraries. Host the container in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use the ECR image in the SageMaker jobs and pipelines.
mcqs.C: Create a SageMaker notebook instance to host the jobs. Create an AWS Lambda function to install the libraries on the notebook instance when the notebook instance starts. Configure the SageMaker jobs and pipelines to run on the notebook instance.
mcqs.D: Run code for the libraries externally on Amazon EC2 instances. Store the results in Amazon S3. Import the results into the SageMaker jobs and pipelines.

explanation: Using a custom Docker container with required libraries hosted in Amazon ECR provides the least implementation effort for using custom libraries in SageMaker jobs and pipelines.

question: An ML engineer is deploying a trained model to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint. The ML engineer needs to receive alerts when data quality issues occur in production. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm and a corresponding action to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification.
mcqs.B: Integrate the SageMaker endpoint with a SageMaker Clarify processing job. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to provide alerts.
mcqs.C: Configure a monitoring job in SageMaker Model Monitor. Integrate Model Monitor with Amazon CloudWatch to provide alerts.
mcqs.D: Configure a data flow in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Integrate Data Wrangler with Amazon CloudWatch to provide alerts.

explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor is used for data quality monitoring in production. It can integrate with CloudWatch for alerts.

question: A company needs to use Amazon SageMaker to train a model on more than 300 GB of data. The training data is composed of files that are 200 MB in size. The data is stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage and feeds a dashboard tool. Which SageMaker training ingestion mechanism is the MOST cost-effective solution for this scenario?

mcqs.A: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system
mcqs.B: Amazon FSx for Lustre file system
mcqs.C: Amazon S3 in fast file mode while using S3 Express One Zone
mcqs.D: Amazon S3 in fast file mode without using S3 Express One Zone

explanation: SageMaker's fast file mode allows for efficient data loading from S3. Without S3 Express One Zone, it remains cost-effective for large datasets like 300+ GB.

question: A company has an ML model that is deployed to an Amazon SageMaker endpoint for real-time inference. The company needs to deploy a new model. The company must compare the new model's performance to the currently deployed model's performance before shifting all traffic to the new model. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

mcqs.A: Deploy the new model to a separate endpoint. Manually split traffic between the two endpoints.
mcqs.B: Deploy the new model to a separate endpoint. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute traffic between the two endpoints.
mcqs.C: Deploy the new model as a shadow variant on the same endpoint as the current model. Route a portion of live traffic to the shadow model for evaluation.
mcqs.D: Use AWS Lambda functions with custom logic to route traffic between the current model and the new model.

explanation: Deploying the new model as a shadow variant on the same endpoint allows for easy comparison with the current model, requiring minimal operational effort.

question: A company runs an ML model on Amazon SageMaker. The company uses an automatic process that makes API calls to create training jobs for the model. The company has new compliance rules that prohibit the collection of aggregated metadata from training jobs. Which solution will prevent SageMaker from collecting metadata from the training jobs?

mcqs.A: Opt out of metadata tracking for any training job that is submitted.
mcqs.B: Ensure that training jobs are running in a private subnet in a custom VPC.
mcqs.C: Encrypt the training data with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.
mcqs.D: Reconfigure the training jobs to use only AWS Nitro instances.

explanation: Opting out of metadata tracking prevents SageMaker from collecting metadata. This is a direct method to comply with the new rules.

question: A company is exploring generative AI and wants to add a new product feature. An ML engineer is making API calls from existing Amazon EC2 instances to Amazon Bedrock. The EC2 instances are in a private subnet and must remain private during the implementation. The EC2 instances have an assigned security group that allows access to all IP addresses in the private subnet. What should the ML engineer do to establish a connection between the EC2 instances and Amazon Bedrock?

mcqs.A: Modify the security group to allow inbound and outbound traffic to and from Amazon Bedrock.
mcqs.B: Use AWS PrivateLink to access Amazon Bedrock through an interface VPC endpoint.
mcqs.C: Configure Amazon Bedrock to use the private subnet where the EC2 instances are deployed.
mcqs.D: Link the existing VPC to Amazon Bedrock by using an AWS Direct Connect connection.

explanation: The ML engineer should use AWS PrivateLink to access Amazon Bedrock through an interface VPC endpoint, allowing private connectivity without exposing the EC2 instances to the public internet.

question: A company wants to launch a new internal generative AI interface to answer user questions. The interface will be based on a popular open source large language model (LLM). Which combination of steps will deploy the interface with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to deploy the LLM.
mcqs.B: Download the LLM as a .zip file. Deploy the LLM on a GPU-based Amazon EC2 instance.
mcqs.C: Create a frontend HTML interface that uses an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API with AWS Lambda functions to handle the user interaction.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon QuickSight to create a UI to handle the user interaction.

explanation: Using SageMaker JumpStart simplifies LLM deployment and API Gateway with Lambda handles user interaction efficiently.

question: A company wants to build a real-time analytics application that uses streaming data from social media. An ML engineer must implement a solution that ingests and transforms 5 GB of data each minute. The solution also must load the data into a data store that supports fast queries for the real-time analytics.

mcqs.A: Use Amazon EventBridge to ingest the social media data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached).
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to ingest the social media data. Use AWS Lambda to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon S3.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the social media data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon RDS.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the social media data. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform the data. Store the transformed data in Amazon DynamoDB.

explanation: Amazon Kinesis and Flink enable real-time data processing. DynamoDB supports fast queries.

question: A company stores training data as a .csv file in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must encrypt the data and must control which applications have access to the encryption key. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a new SSH access key. Use the AWS Encryption CLI with a reference to the new access key to encrypt the file.
mcqs.B: Create a new API key by using the Amazon API Gateway CreateApiKey API operation. Use the AWS CLI with a reference to the new API key to encrypt the file.
mcqs.C: Create a new IAM role. Attach a policy that allows the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) GenerateDataKey action. Use the role to encrypt the file.
mcqs.D: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use the AWS Encryption CLI with a reference to the new KMS key to encrypt the file.

explanation: Using a customer-managed KMS key allows full control over encryption and access policies. This meets the requirements for encrypting data and controlling access to the encryption key.

question: A company needs to perform feature engineering, aggregation, and data preparation. After the features are produced, the company must implement a solution on AWS to process and store the features. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Feature Processing to process and ingest the data. Use SageMaker Feature Store to manage and store the features.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor to automatically ingest and transform the data. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the features in JSON format.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform the data and to ingest the data directly into Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. Use Feature Store to manage and store the features.
mcqs.D: Use an Amazon SageMaker batch transform job to analyze, transform, and ingest the data. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the features.

explanation: SageMaker Feature Store provides both offline and online feature access. This meets the requirements for processing and storing features.

question: A company is developing a new online application to gather information from customers. An ML engineer has developed a new ML model that will determine a score for each customer. The model will use the score to determine which product to display to the customer. The ML engineer needs to minimize response-time latency for the model. How should the ML engineer deploy the application in Amazon SageMaker to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Configure batch transform.
mcqs.B: Configure a real-time inference endpoint.
mcqs.C: Configure a serverless inference endpoint.
mcqs.D: Configure an asynchronous inference endpoint.

explanation: To minimize response-time latency, a real-time inference endpoint is suitable as it provides immediate responses. This approach is ideal for applications requiring low latency and high throughput. It directly supports the use case of displaying products based on customer scores.

question: A company is using Amazon EMR. The company has a large dataset in Amazon S3 that needs to be ingested into Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. The dataset contains historical data and real-time streaming data. The company must ensure that the Feature Store online store is updated with the most recent data as soon as the data becomes available. The company also must maintain a complete Feature Store offline store for batch processing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use the PutRecord API in Feature Store Runtime to ingest all the data into the online store.
mcqs.B: Use the PutRecord API in Feature Store Runtime to ingest all the data into the offline store.
mcqs.C: Use the Feature Store Spark connector to ingest the data as Spark DataFrames with the online store and offline store enabled.
mcqs.D: Use the Feature Store Spark connector to ingest the data as Spark DataFrames with only the online store enabled.

explanation: The Feature Store Spark connector allows ingesting data into both online and offline stores, meeting the requirements for real-time and batch processing.

question: An ML engineer needs to deploy four ML models in an Amazon SageMaker inference pipeline. The models were built with different frameworks. The ML engineer also needs to give clients the ability to use the invoke_endpoint call to perform inference for each model. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

mcqs.A: Create a SageMaker multi-model endpoint.
mcqs.B: Create a SageMaker multi-container endpoint.
mcqs.C: Create multiple SageMaker single-model endpoints.
mcqs.D: Run a SparkML job to generate multiple endpoints.

explanation: SageMaker multi-container endpoints support up to 15 containers for complex inference workflows, making it suitable for deploying multiple models built with different frameworks.

question: An ML engineer wants an Amazon SageMaker notebook to automatically stop running after 1 hour of idle time. How can the ML engineer accomplish this goal?

mcqs.A: Create a lifecycle configuration in SageMaker. Copy the auto-stop-idle script from GitHub to the Start Notebook section.
mcqs.B: Create a lifecycle configuration in SageMaker. Copy the auto-stop-idle script from GitHub to the Create Notebook section.
mcqs.C: Track the notebook's CPU metric by using Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from CloudWatch Logs to shut down the notebook instance if CPU utilization becomes zero.
mcqs.D: Track the notebook's memory metric by using Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from CloudWatch Logs to shut down the notebook instance if memory utilization becomes zero.

explanation: SageMaker lifecycle configurations can be used to automatically stop notebook instances after a specified idle period. This is done by copying an auto-stop-idle script to the Start Notebook section.

question: A company wants to provide services to help other businesses label images. The company wants its labeling specialists to complete human labeling tasks on AWS. How should the company register the labeling specialists to receive tasks on AWS?

mcqs.A: Use AWS Data Exchange.
mcqs.B: Create and use an internal workforce in Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.
mcqs.C: Create and use Amazon Mechanical Turk entities in an Amazon SageMaker human loop.
mcqs.D: Use the Amazon Mechanical Turk website.

explanation: The company should use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to create and manage an internal workforce for labeling tasks. This allows for custom UI templates, quality controls, and annotation workflows for image labeling at scale.

question: A company wants to use Amazon SageMaker to host an ML model that runs on CPU for real-time predictions. The model will have intermittent traffic during business hours and will have periods of no traffic after business hours. The company needs a solution that will serve inference requests in the most cost-effective manner. Which hosting option will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Deploy the model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Add a schedule-based auto scaling policy to handle traffic surges during business hours.
mcqs.B: Deploy the model to a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint. Configure increased provisioned concurrency during business hours.
mcqs.C: Deploy the model to a SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint. Configure an auto scaling policy that scales in to zero outside business hours.
mcqs.D: Deploy the model to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that activates the endpoint during business hours only.

explanation: SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint automatically scales to match traffic, making it cost-effective for intermittent traffic. This option eliminates the need to manage servers and scales to zero when not in use.

question: An ML engineer needs to train a supervised deep learning model. The available dataset is a large number of unlabeled images that only employees should access. The ML engineer needs to implement a solution that labels the dataset with the highest possible accuracy. Which combination of steps should the ML engineer take to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Rekognition to automatically label the dataset.
mcqs.B: Train the deep learning model directly on the raw data. Let the model infer the labels by itself.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to create an annotation job that specifies the labeling task and requirements.
mcqs.D: Set up workforce teams to access a private workforce to run and review the annotation job created by Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth.

explanation: The ML engineer should use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to create an annotation job for labeling and set up a private workforce for accurate labeling.

question: A company is using an Amazon S3 bucket to collect data that will be used for ML workflows. The company needs to use AWS Glue DataBrew to clean and normalize the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a DataBrew dataset by using the S3 path. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew profile job.
mcqs.B: Create a DataBrew dataset by using the S3 path. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew recipe job.
mcqs.C: Create a DataBrew dataset by using a Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver to connect to the S3 bucket. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew profile job.
mcqs.D: Create a DataBrew dataset by using a Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) driver to connect to the S3 bucket. Clean and normalize the data by using a DataBrew recipe job.

explanation: To use AWS Glue DataBrew for cleaning and normalizing data from an S3 bucket, a DataBrew dataset should be created using the S3 path. Then, a DataBrew recipe job is used for data cleaning and normalization, making option B the correct choice.

question: A company is developing a new ML model that uses the XGBoost algorithm. The company will train the model on data that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is in a nested JSON format. An ML engineer needs to convert the JSON files into a tabular format. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Create an AWS Glue PySpark job that uses the Relationalize transform to convert the files.
mcqs.B: Write custom Scala code to convert the files. Use Amazon EMR Serverless to run the Scala code.
mcqs.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses a Python runtime and invokes the reduce() function to convert the files. Invoke the Lambda function.
mcqs.D: Create an Amazon Athena database that is based on the JSON files. Use the Athena flatten function to convert the data.

explanation: AWS Glue provides a managed service for ETL operations, and its Relationalize transform can easily flatten nested JSON data into a tabular format with minimal code.

question: A medical company ingests streams of data from devices that monitor patients' vital signs. The company uses Amazon SageMaker and plans to prepare ML models to predict adverse events for patients. The dataset is large with thousands of features. An ML engineer needs to run several hundred training iterations with different sets of features, different algorithms, and many potential parameters. The ML engineer must implement a solution to log the characteristics and results of each training iteration. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to create custom metrics for the characteristics of each iteration.
mcqs.B: Write the characteristics of each iteration to logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue and Amazon Athena to search the logs.
mcqs.C: Use the SageMaker Model Registry to track the characteristics and results of each iteration.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Experiments to track the characteristics and results of each iteration.

explanation: SageMaker Experiments is a built-in feature that allows tracking and comparison of training iterations, making it the most efficient solution.

question: A company is planning to create an internal-only chat interface to help employees handle customer queries. Currently, the employees need to refer to a massive knowledge base of internal documents to address customer issues. The new solution must be serverless. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Set up Amazon Bedrock with the Anthropic Claude foundation model.
mcqs.B: Set up Amazon SageMaker JumpStart with the Llama foundation model.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon API Gateway to invoke the model API.
mcqs.D: Use AWS Lambda functions with Amazon API Gateway to invoke the model API.

explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides serverless foundation models and AWS Lambda functions enable serverless API invocation.

question: An ML engineer needs to deploy a trained model that is based on a genetic algorithm. The algorithm solves a complex problem and can take several minutes to generate predictions. When the model is deployed, the model needs to access large amounts of data to process requests. The requests can involve as much as 100 MB of data. Which deployment solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Deploy the model to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
mcqs.B: Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint.
mcqs.C: Deploy the model to an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint.
mcqs.D: Package the model as a container. Deploy the model to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 instances.

explanation: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint is suitable for long-running predictions with large data inputs, reducing operational overhead compared to managing EC2 instances or ECS.

question: An ML engineer wants to use a set of survey responses as training data for an ML classifier. All the survey responses are either yes or no. The ML engineer needs to convert the responses into a feature that will produce better model training results. The ML engineer must not increase the dimensionality of the dataset. Which methods will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

mcqs.A: Binary encoding
mcqs.B: Label encoding
mcqs.C: One-hot encoding
mcqs.D: Statistical imputation

explanation: Binary encoding and label encoding do not increase dimensionality for binary responses.

question: A company has several teams that have developed separate prediction models on their own laptops. The teams developed the models by using Python with scikit-learn and TensorFlow frameworks. The company must rebuild the models and must integrate the models into an ML infrastructure that the company manages by using Amazon SageMaker. The company also must incorporate the models into a model registry. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Export the models from the laptops to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions with SageMaker endpoints to access the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
mcqs.B: Import the models into the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker to run the imported models.
mcqs.C: Use code from the laptops to create containers for the models. Use the bring your own container (BYOC) functionality of SageMaker to import and use the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
mcqs.D: Import the Python-based models into SageMaker. Rebuild the scikit-learn and TensorFlow models in SageMaker. Register all the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.

explanation: Using the bring your own container (BYOC) functionality of SageMaker allows for seamless integration of existing models with minimal operational overhead.

question: A company is training a large language model (LLM) by using on-premises infrastructure. A live conversational engine uses the LLM to help customers find real-time insights in credit card data. An ML engineer must implement a solution to train and deploy the LLM on Amazon SageMaker. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Training Compiler to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker with deep learning containers for large model inference to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Notebook Jobs to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker Asynchronous Inference.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Studio to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker batch transform.

explanation: SageMaker Training Compiler can optimize and train large models efficiently. Deploying with SageMaker real-time inference allows for immediate responses, suitable for live conversational engines. This approach supports the requirements for both training and deploying the LLM.

question: A company has an existing Amazon SageMaker model on a production endpoint. The company develops a new model version and needs to test the new version in production before substituting it for the existing model. The company needs to implement a solution to minimize the risk of the new model generating incorrect output in production. The solution must prevent any disruption of production traffic during the change to the new model. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a second production variant for the new model. Assign 1% of the traffic to the new model and 99% of the traffic to the existing model. Collect all the output of the new model in an Amazon S3 bucket. If the new model performs as expected, switch all the traffic to the new model.
mcqs.B: Create a second production variant for the new model. Assign 10% of the traffic to the new model and 90% of the traffic to the existing model. Collect all the output of the new model in an Amazon S3 bucket. If the new model performs as expected, switch all the traffic to the new model.
mcqs.C: Deploy the new model to a new endpoint. Turn on data capturing for the production endpoint. Write a script to pass 100% of input data to the new model. If the new model performs as expected, deactivate the existing model endpoint and direct the traffic to the new model.
mcqs.D: Deploy the new model into a shadow variant that samples 100% of the inference requests. Collect all the output in an Amazon S3 bucket. If the new model performs as expected, promote it to production.

explanation: This solution allows for testing the new model without disrupting production traffic. The shadow variant tests the new model with 100% of requests without affecting the existing model.

question: A company is building an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker, AWS owned libraries, and open source libraries. The company must ensure that SageMaker does not collect metadata about usage and errors during training. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Associate the SageMaker domain with a custom IAM role. Attach the role to a policy that denies Amazon CloudWatch service usage logs.
mcqs.B: Add an IAM role to the SageMaker domain to deny Amazon CloudWatch the permission to report metadata.
mcqs.C: Turn off the setting in the SageMaker domain to share metadata for console jobs. Opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs.
mcqs.D: Set a parameter to opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI, Boto3, or the SageMaker Python SDK.
