explanation: To prevent SageMaker from collecting metadata, the setting to share metadata for console jobs needs to be turned off and metadata collection needs to be opted out for each training job.

question: An ML engineer is training an ML model to identify people's health risk based on 20 features and 1 target. The target class has two values: Likely to have health risk (positive class) and Unlikely to have health risk (negative class). The age range of people in the dataset is 30 years old to 60 years old. Age is one of the features. The ML engineer analyzes the features. For the positive class, the difference in proportions of labels (DPL) value is (+0.9) for the age range of 40 to 45 compared with all other age ranges. What should the ML engineer do to correct this data imbalance?

mcqs.A: Oversample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
mcqs.B: Undersample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
mcqs.C: Undersample the positive class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.
mcqs.D: Oversample the negative class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.

explanation: To correct the data imbalance, the ML engineer should undersample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45, as it has a significantly higher proportion of positive labels compared to other age ranges.

question: A company is building an Amazon SageMaker AI pipeline for an ML model. The pipeline uses distributed processing and training. An ML engineer needs to encrypt network communication between instances that run distributed jobs. The ML engineer configures the distributed jobs to run in a private VPC. What should the ML engineer do to meet the encryption requirement?

mcqs.A: Enable network isolation.
mcqs.B: Configure traffic encryption by using security groups.
mcqs.C: Enable inter-container traffic encryption.
mcqs.D: Enable VPC flow logs.

explanation: To encrypt network communication between instances for distributed jobs in SageMaker, enabling inter-container traffic encryption is the appropriate action. This ensures data exchanged between containers during distributed training is encrypted.

question: An ML model is deployed in production. The model has performed well and has met its metric thresholds for months. An ML engineer who is monitoring the model observes a sudden degradation. The performance metrics of the model are now below the thresholds. What could be the cause of the performance degradation?

mcqs.A: Lack of training data
mcqs.B: Drift in production data distribution
mcqs.C: Compute resource constraints
mcqs.D: Model overfitting

explanation: The sudden degradation in model performance could be due to a change in the data distribution. This is a common issue in deployed models.

question: An ML engineer is using AWS Glue to transform proprietary data from a third-party vendor to a format that the ML engineer intends to use with the Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm. The data includes several similar time series data files that the ML engineer must convert to the appropriate format. The ML engineer must compress the files to optimize storage costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Snappy to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
mcqs.B: Use XZ to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
mcqs.C: Use XZ to convert the files to Apache Parquet format and to compress the files.
mcqs.D: Use gzip to convert the files to Apache Parquet and to compress the files.

explanation: Apache Parquet is a suitable format for Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm. XZ is a compression algorithm that can be used with Parquet.

question: A company has significantly increased the amount of data that is stored as .csv files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Data transformation scripts and queries are now taking much longer than they used to take. An ML engineer must implement a solution to optimize the data for query performance. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Configure an AWS Lambda function to split the .csv files into smaller objects in the S3 bucket.
mcqs.B: Configure an AWS Glue job to drop columns that have string type values and to save the results to the S3 bucket.
mcqs.C: Configure an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Apache Parquet format.
mcqs.D: Configure an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data that is in the S3 bucket.

explanation: Converting CSV to Parquet format optimizes data for query performance by enabling columnar storage, which reduces storage costs and improves query performance with column pruning and predicate pushdown.

question: An ML engineer is analyzing a classification dataset before training a model in Amazon SageMaker AI. The ML engineer suspects that the dataset has a significant imbalance between class labels that could lead to biased model predictions. To confirm class imbalance, the ML engineer needs to select an appropriate pre-training bias metric. Which metric will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Mean square error (MSE)
mcqs.B: Difference in proportions of labels (DPL)
mcqs.C: Silhouette score
mcqs.D: Structural similarity index measure (SSIM)

explanation: The Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL) is a suitable metric for detecting class imbalance in a dataset. It measures the difference in proportions of labels between the dataset and the ideal balanced distribution. This helps in identifying biased datasets.

question: An ML engineer uses one ML framework to train multiple ML models. The ML engineer needs to optimize the inference costs and host the models on Amazon SageMaker AI. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

mcqs.A: Create a multi-container inference endpoint for direct invocation.
mcqs.B: Create a multi-model inference endpoint for all the models.
mcqs.C: Create a multi-container inference endpoint for sequential invocation.
mcqs.D: Create multiple single-model inference endpoint for each model.

explanation: A multi-model inference endpoint allows hosting multiple models on a single endpoint, reducing costs compared to creating separate endpoints for each model.

question: A company is using an ML model to classify motion in videos. The data is stored in MP4 format in Amazon S3. When the company created the model, the company needed 4 months to label all the video frames. The company needs to retrain the model with an existing training workflow in Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer must implement a solution that decreases the labeling time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Ground Truth to annotate the video frames.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker JumpStart to use pre-trained computer vision models to develop a labeling model.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to create a data workflow. Use the workflow to optimize the labeling process.
mcqs.D: Use the labeling interface of Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) with Amazon Rekognition to label the video frames.

explanation: Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I) can be used with Amazon Rekognition to label video frames, reducing manual labeling effort.

question: An ecommerce company trains an ML model to forecast demand for near real-time inventory management based on historical customer activity. The company successfully deploys the trained model to a production Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. However, the company notices that the model's forecast performance degrades over time. The company needs a long-term and automated solution to mitigate the performance degradation. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to automatically send alerts when model performance anomalies are detected.
mcqs.B: Use AWS X-Ray to monitor the performance of the SageMaker AI endpoint and the incoming requests to inform model re-training.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth to curate a high-quality dataset. Use the dataset to re-train the model.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to monitor model and feature attribution bias to inform model re-training.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Debugger can automatically detect model performance anomalies, making it suitable for long-term and automated mitigation of performance degradation.

question: A logistics company wants to improve driver safety by identifying distractions that could lead to accidents. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Rekognition eye gaze direction detection to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon SageMaker AI to customize an AI model to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
mcqs.C: Integrate a third-party driver monitoring system with Amazon Rekognition to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze text-based driver feedback and identify distractions.

explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides pre-trained computer vision APIs for face detection, object detection, and video analysis, enabling rapid deployment without custom model training. This requires the least operational effort.

question: A company has trained an ML model that is packaged in a container. The company will integrate the model with an existing Python web application. The company needs to host the model on AWS by using Kubernetes. The company does not want to manage the control plane and must provision the resources in a repeatable manner. The infrastructure must be provisioned by using Python. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use AWS CloudFormation to provision Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Set up a Kubernetes cluster. Host the model container on the Kubernetes cluster.
mcqs.B: Use the AWS CLI to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.
mcqs.C: Use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.
mcqs.D: Use AWS CloudFormation to provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Store the image in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Host the model container on the EKS cluster.

explanation: The AWS CDK allows for repeatable and programmatic infrastructure provisioning using Python. EKS manages the control plane, meeting the requirement of not managing it.

question: An ML engineer is developing a linear regression ML model. The model shows high accuracy on the training dataset but performs poorly on unseen new data. Which action should the ML engineer take to address this issue?

mcqs.A: Increase the complexity of the model to capture more patterns in the training data. Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to monitor for convergence issues.
mcqs.B: Apply ML techniques such as cross-validation and regularization. Use Amazon SageMaker Experiments to track and compare different model versions and their performance metrics.
mcqs.C: Directly deploy the model into production. Use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to interpret model outputs on new data. Adjust the model based on these insights.
mcqs.D: Increase the size of the training dataset without adjusting the size of the model. Retrain the model on the new data. Generate a confusion matrix to analyze the results.

explanation: The issue described is overfitting. Applying techniques like cross-validation and regularization can help improve the model's generalization to unseen data.

question: A company is training a new ML model to replace a model that is deployed on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. An ML engineer needs to determine the latency and the accuracy of the new model. The ML engineer must evaluate the new model in a production scenario without affecting the users of the existing model. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Perform a blue/green deployment with linear traffic shifting.
mcqs.B: Perform a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting.
mcqs.C: Perform a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size of 50% of the current fleet.
mcqs.D: Perform shadow testing with a traffic sampling percentage of 100%.

explanation: SageMaker shadow testing allows evaluation of a new model without affecting users of the existing model.

question: An ML engineer wants to use, prepare, and load data from Amazon S3 for analytics. The ML engineer must run an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to discover the schema of the data and to store the metadata. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST manual effort?

mcqs.A: Use AWS Glue to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog.
mcqs.B: Create an Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in an S3 bucket.
mcqs.C: Create an ETL pipeline by using Amazon Athena integrated with AWS Step Functions. Use the pipeline to run the ETL job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in an S3 bucket.
mcqs.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that includes the scikit-learn library to run the ETL job. Use the job to discover the schema and to store the associated metadata in Amazon Redshift.

explanation: AWS Glue provides a fully managed ETL service that can automatically discover schema and store metadata in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, requiring minimal manual effort.

question: An ML engineer is building an ML pipeline. The pipeline must process a dataset in two ways by using Amazon Athena. The pipeline must use batch processing to perform large-scale data transformations and for model training. The pipeline must also use near real-time processing to perform low-latency queries for inference and analytics. Which file format will provide the LEAST latency for both types of processing?

mcqs.A: CSV
mcqs.B: Apache Parquet
mcqs.C: Nested JSON
mcqs.D: Deserialized JSON

explanation: Apache Parquet is a columnar storage format that provides efficient compression and encoding schemes, making it suitable for both batch and near real-time processing with low latency.

question: A company uses an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to make real-time inferences. The company has configured auto scaling for the Amazon EC2 instances that SageMaker AI uses for the inferences. During times of peak usage, new instances launch before existing instances are fully ready. As a result, the model experiences inefficiencies and delays. Which solution will optimize the scaling process without affecting response times?

mcqs.A: Change to a multi-model endpoint configuration in SageMaker AI.
mcqs.B: Integrate Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to manage invocations of the SageMaker AI inference endpoint.
mcqs.C: Decrease the cooldown period for scale-in activities. Increase the maximum number of instances.
mcqs.D: Increase the cooldown period after scale-out activities.

explanation: Increasing the cooldown period after scale-out activities allows existing instances to be fully utilized before new instances are launched, optimizing the scaling process without affecting response times.

question: A company deployed an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to an endpoint. The network that was established includes two private subnets and one security group. The model must download data from an Amazon S3 bucket and must upload data to the S3 bucket. The traffic to the S3 bucket must not travel across the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the security group to allow outbound connections. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the NAT gateway.
mcqs.B: Create a gateway VPC endpoint. Configure an endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.
mcqs.C: Create an interface VPC endpoint. Verify that the security group allows only inbound connections. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.
mcqs.D: Create a Gateway Load Balancer VPC endpoint. Configure an IAM policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket. Configure route tables to redirect any traffic to the S3 bucket through the endpoint.

explanation: A gateway VPC endpoint allows traffic to S3 without traversing the internet. Configuring an endpoint policy restricts access to the S3 bucket.

question: A company is developing a new ML model to rank customers in order of their potential to pay back loans. The company needs to use an Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithm. Which algorithm should the company use to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: XGBoost
mcqs.B: K-means clustering
mcqs.C: Principal component analysis (PCA)
mcqs.D: Neural Topic Model (NTM)

explanation: XGBoost is suitable for ranking tasks as it outputs a continuous score that can be used to rank customers by their loan repayment probability.

question: An ML engineer is setting up an Amazon SageMaker AI pipeline for an ML model. The pipeline must automatically initiate a re-training job if any data drift is detected.

mcqs.A: Use an AWS Glue crawler and an AWS Glue extract, transform and load (ETL) job to detect data drift. Use AWS Glue triggers to automate the re-training job.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to detect data drift. Use an AWS Lambda function to automate the re-training job.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to detect data drift. Use an AWS Lambda function to automate the re-training job.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon QuickSight anomaly detection to detect data drift. Use an AWS Step Functions workflow to automate the re-training job.

explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor detects data drift and can trigger a re-training job via AWS Lambda.

question: A company has developed a computer vision model. The company needs to deploy the model into production on Amazon SageMaker AI. The company has not hosted a model on SageMaker AI previously. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to track model versions. The solution also must provide recommendations about which Amazon EC2 instance types to use to host the model.

mcqs.A: Register the model in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use AWS Compute Optimizer for recommendations about instance types.
mcqs.B: Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker Autopilot for recommendations about instance types.
mcqs.C: Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker Inference Recommender for recommendations about instance types.
mcqs.D: Register the model in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Use SageMaker Experiments for recommendations about instance types.

explanation: The SageMaker Model Registry is used for tracking model versions. SageMaker Inference Recommender provides recommendations on EC2 instance types for hosting models.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to develop a credit risk assessment model. During model validation, the company finds that the model achieves 82% accuracy on the validation data. However, the model achieved 99% accuracy on the training data. The company needs to address the model accuracy issue before deployment. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Add more dense layers to increase model complexity. Implement batch normalization. Use early stopping during training.
mcqs.B: Implement dropout layers. Use L1 or L2 regularization. Perform k-fold cross-validation.
mcqs.C: Use principal component analysis (PCA) to reduce the feature dimensionality. Decrease model layers. Implement cross-entropy loss functions.
mcqs.D: Augment the training dataset. Remove duplicate records from the training dataset. Implement stratified sampling.

explanation: The model is overfitting, indicated by high training accuracy and low validation accuracy. Implementing dropout layers, L1 or L2 regularization, and k-fold cross-validation can help prevent overfitting and improve model generalization.

question: A company collects customer data every day. The company stores the data as compressed files in an Amazon S3 bucket that is partitioned by date. Every month, analysts download the data, process the data to check the data quality, and then upload the data to Amazon QuickSight dashboards. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to automatically check the data quality before the data is sent to QuickSight. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Run an AWS Glue crawler every month to update the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use AWS Glue Data Quality rules to check the data quality.
mcqs.B: Use an AWS Glue trigger to run an AWS Glue crawler every month to update the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Create an AWS Glue job that loads the data into a PySpark DataFrame. Configure the job to apply custom functions and to evaluate the data quality.
mcqs.C: Run Python scripts on an AWS Lambda function every month to evaluate data quality. Configure the S3 bucket to invoke the Lambda function when objects are added to the S3 bucket.
mcqs.D: Configure the S3 bucket to send event notifications to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when objects are uploaded. Use Amazon CloudWatch insights every month for the SQS queue to evaluate the data quality.

explanation: AWS Glue Data Quality rules provide a managed solution to check data quality with minimal operational overhead.

question: A company has an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. An ML engineer needs to implement a monitoring solution to automatically detect changes in the input data distribution of model features. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor. Establish a data quality baseline. Ensure that the emit_metrics option is enabled in the baseline constraints file. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the company about changes in specific metrics that are related to data quality.
mcqs.B: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor. Establish a model quality baseline. Ensure that the comparison_method option is set to Robust in the baseline constraints file. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the company about changes in model quality metrics.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Debugger with custom rules to track shifts in feature distributions. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify the company when the rules detect significant changes.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon CloudWatch to directly observe the SageMaker AI endpoint's performance metrics. Manually analyze the CloudWatch logs for indicators of data drift or shifts in feature distribution.

explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor detects changes in input data distribution with minimal operational overhead.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to deploy a new recommendation model for its ecommerce website. The model must use data from all client website interactions as input. Traffic is variable throughout the day. The company needs to create an inference endpoint for the model. Which type of inference endpoint will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

mcqs.A: Batch transform inference endpoint
mcqs.B: Asynchronous inference endpoint
mcqs.C: Real-time inference endpoint
mcqs.D: Serverless inference endpoint

explanation: Serverless inference endpoint is the most cost-effective option for variable traffic and large data inputs.

question: A company's ML engineer is creating a classification model. The ML engineer explores the dataset and notices a column that is named day_of_week. The column's data consists of the following values: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. Which technique should the ML engineer use to convert this column's data to binary values?

mcqs.A: Binary encoding
mcqs.B: Label encoding
mcqs.C: One-hot encoding
mcqs.D: Tokenization

explanation: One-hot encoding is suitable for categorical features like day_of_week. It converts each category into a binary vector, avoiding ordinal relationships between categories.

question: An ML engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to prepare data for training. During exploratory data analysis, the ML engineer notices that several categorical features are missing values. How can the ML engineer use SageMaker AI to solve this problem?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to impute categorical features with the mean value.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Clarify to impute categorical features with the mode value.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mean value.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mode value.

explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler is suitable for data preparation and can impute categorical features with the mode value. Mean imputation is typically used for numerical features.

question: A company stores user clickstream data in an Amazon S3 bucket in AWS Account A. The company needs to use the data to train an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI in AWS Account B. The training will take 10 days. The company needs to use only private IP addresses in the training. The company also must make sure that no training metadata is shared with AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Set up VPC peering between Account A and Account B. Contact AWS by email to opt out of metadata collection.
mcqs.B: Set up a VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket. Set the SageMaker AI OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable to 1 in the training job.
mcqs.C: Configure a security group policy that is assigned to the S3 bucket in Account A to allow access from only Account B. Create AI services opt-out policies.
mcqs.D: Generate presigned URLs with expiration times for the objects that are stored in the S3 bucket. Access the data by using the presigned URLs. Set the SageMaker AI OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable to 1 in the training job.

explanation: Using a VPC endpoint allows private IP access. Setting the SageMaker AI OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable to 1 prevents metadata sharing.

question: A music streaming company constantly streams song ratings from an application to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to use the ratings as an input for training and inference of an Amazon SageMaker AI model. The company has an AWS Glue Data Catalog that is configured with the S3 bucket as the source. An ML engineer needs to implement a solution to create a repository for this data. The solution must ensure that the data stays synchronized during batch training and real-time inference. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Ingest data into SageMaker Feature Store from the S3 bucket. Apply tags and indexes.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Athena. Create tables by using CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) queries to group data.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Lake Formation. Apply tag-based control on the data.
mcqs.D: Use the Generate Data Insights function in SageMaker Data Wrangler.

explanation: SageMaker Feature Store provides a centralized repository for storing and managing features that can be used for both batch training and real-time inference. This ensures data synchronization across different stages of the machine learning workflow.

question: A hospital is using an ML model to validate x-ray results. The hospital runs a nightly batch inference job. The hospital needs to produce a daily report about model data quality and model performance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Schedule a monitoring job in Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor. Generate the monitoring results for the model and data.
mcqs.B: Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that includes the metrics for processing steps in the nightly batch inference job. Compare the baseline resource metrics. Share the dashboard link.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a custom recipe job that uses the Numerical Statistics data quality check for the model file. Generate the results.
mcqs.D: Create a SageMaker AI pipeline that includes a QualityCheck step to run monitoring jobs. Generate the monitoring results for the model and the data.

explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor is used for monitoring data quality and model performance. It can be scheduled to generate daily reports.

question: A company needs to ingest data from data sources into Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler. The data sources are Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Snowflake. The ingested data must always be up to date with the latest changes in the source systems. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use direct connections to import data from the data sources into Data Wrangler.
mcqs.B: Use cataloged connections to import data from the data sources into Data Wrangler.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue to extract data from the data sources. Use AWS Glue also to import the data directly into Data Wrangler.
mcqs.D: Use AWS Lambda to extract data from the data sources. Use Lambda also to import the data directly into Data Wrangler.

explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler supports cataloged connections to keep data up to date with the latest changes in source systems.

question: An ML engineer is using Amazon SageMaker Canvas to build a custom ML model from an imported dataset. The ML engineer wants the model to make continuous numeric predictions based on 10 years of data. Which metric should the ML engineer use to evaluate the model's performance?

mcqs.A: Accuracy
mcqs.B: InferenceLatency
mcqs.C: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
mcqs.D: Root mean square error (RMSE)

explanation: For continuous numeric predictions, RMSE is a suitable metric. It measures the square root of the average squared differences between predicted and actual values.

question: A company has built, trained, and tuned two new ML models: Model A detects if a transaction is fraudulent based on the IP address, location, and user credentials. This model will be accessed every time a transaction occurs. Model B forecasts sales totals for the next month based on historical sales data. This model will be accessed one time each month. The company must deploy both models to production by using Amazon SageMaker AI. Which hosting solution for the models should the company use to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Host both models in one container behind one real-time endpoint.
mcqs.B: Host Model A with an asynchronous endpoint. Host Model B with a real-time endpoint.
mcqs.C: Host Model A with a real-time endpoint. Use batch transform for Model B.
mcqs.D: Use batch transform for Model A. Host Model B with an asynchronous endpoint.

explanation: Model A requires real-time processing for fraud detection, while Model B can be used for batch processing for sales forecasting. Hosting Model A with a real-time endpoint and using batch transform for Model B meets the requirements.

question: A bank needs to use Amazon SageMaker AI to create an ML model to determine which customers qualify for a new product. The bank must use algorithms that SageMaker AI directly supports. The model must be explainable to the bank's regulators. Which modeling approach will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Train the model by using the Object2Vec algorithm.
mcqs.B: Train the model by using the linear learner algorithm.
mcqs.C: Train a neural network.
mcqs.D: Train the model by using the k-means algorithm.

explanation: The linear learner algorithm in SageMaker provides explainable models, which is a requirement for regulated industries like banking. This algorithm is also directly supported by SageMaker.

question: An ML engineer is building a model to predict house and apartment prices. The model uses three features: Square Meters, Price, and Age of Building. The dataset has 10,000 data rows. The data includes data points for one large mansion and one extremely small apartment. The ML engineer must perform preprocessing on the dataset to ensure that the model produces accurate predictions for the typical house or apartment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Remove the outliers and perform a log transformation on the Square Meters variable.
mcqs.B: Keep the outliers and perform normalization on the Square Meters variable.
mcqs.C: Remove the outliers and perform one-hot encoding on the Square Meters variable.
mcqs.D: Keep the outliers and perform one-hot encoding on the Square Meters variable.

explanation: Removing outliers like the large mansion and extremely small apartment helps prevent them from skewing the model. Log transformation on the Square Meters variable can help normalize the distribution if it's right-skewed. This approach improves the model's accuracy for typical houses and apartments.

question: A company is developing an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The company must monitor bias in the model and must display the results on a dashboard. An ML engineer creates a bias monitoring job. How should the ML engineer capture bias metrics to display on the dashboard?

mcqs.A: Capture AWS CloudTrail metrics from SageMaker Clarify.
mcqs.B: Capture Amazon CloudWatch metrics from SageMaker Clarify.
mcqs.C: Capture SageMaker Model Monitor metrics from Amazon EventBridge.
mcqs.D: Capture SageMaker Model Monitor metrics from Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

explanation: The ML engineer should capture Amazon CloudWatch metrics from SageMaker Clarify to monitor bias and display results on a dashboard.

question: A company is using an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to predict traffic accidents that potholes cause. An ML engineer has configured SageMaker Model Monitor to run as part of a SageMaker AI pipeline. In the MonitoringExecution output, the ML engineer observes several baseline_drift_check violations that are failing the pipeline. What should the ML engineer do to resolve this issue?

mcqs.A: Retrain the model by using a new SageMaker AI training job. Check for errors by using SageMaker Debugger.
mcqs.B: Retrain the model with new training data. Reuse the original baseline in Model Monitor.
mcqs.C: Retrain the model with new training data. Use the new baseline in Model Monitor.
mcqs.D: Rerun the SageMaker AI pipeline after enabling the emit_metrics option in the baseline constraints file.

explanation: The ML engineer should retrain the model with new training data and use a new baseline in Model Monitor to resolve baseline drift issues.

question: A company uses ML models to predict whether transactions are fraudulent. The company needs to identify as many fraudulent transactions as possible. Which evaluation metric should the company use to evaluate the models to meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: F1 score
mcqs.B: Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)
mcqs.C: Precision
mcqs.D: Recall

explanation: To identify as many fraudulent transactions as possible, the company should focus on maximizing the number of true positives. Recall is the metric that measures the proportion of actual positives that are correctly identified, making it the most suitable choice.

question: An ML engineer has trained an ML model using Amazon SageMaker AI. The ML engineer determines that the model is overfitting and that the training data contains unnecessary features. The ML engineer must reduce the overfitting and the impact of the unnecessary features. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Increase the number of training iterations. Retrain the model.
mcqs.B: Apply L1 regularization to the training data. Retrain the model.
mcqs.C: Decrease the number of training iterations. Retrain the model.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker Debugger to apply L1 regularization to the running model.

explanation: Applying L1 regularization reduces overfitting by adding a penalty term to the loss function for large weights, and it can set some model coefficients to zero, effectively removing unnecessary features.

question: An ML engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to perform preprocessing on a dataset. The ML engineer wants to use the processed dataset to train a classification model. During preprocessing, the ML engineer notices that a text feature has a range of thousands of values that differ only by spelling errors. The ML engineer needs to apply an encoding method so that after preprocessing is complete, the text feature can be used to train the model. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Perform ordinal encoding to represent categories of the feature.
mcqs.B: Perform similarity encoding to represent categories of the feature.
mcqs.C: Perform one-hot encoding to represent categories of the feature.
mcqs.D: Perform target encoding to represent categories of the feature.

explanation: Similarity encoding is suitable for text features with minor variations like spelling errors, allowing the model to recognize similarities.

question: An ML engineer is training a text generation model on Amazon SageMaker AI. After several epochs, the loss function does not converge, and the model's accuracy on the validation dataset starts to show oscillating results. The ML engineer needs to ensure that the model achieves generalization.

mcqs.A: Increase the learning rate and decrease the mini-batch size.
mcqs.B: Increase the learning rate as the number of epochs increases.
mcqs.C: Decrease the learning rate and increase the mini-batch size.
mcqs.D: Decrease the learning rate and decrease the mini-batch size.

explanation: Decreasing the learning rate can help the model converge, while increasing the mini-batch size can improve stability and generalization.

question: A company uses an NFS-based data store to store data for ML training. Linux-based systems access the data store. The company needs a hybrid system to make the shared data store accessible to on-premises servers and Amazon SageMaker AI notebooks that will consume the data. File locking is required for the data producers. Which AWS storage solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the data. Use Mountpoint for Amazon S3 to mount the S3 bucket to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
mcqs.B: Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the data. Mount the file system to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
mcqs.C: Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to store the data. Mount the file system to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.
mcqs.D: Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to store the data. Mount the volume to the on-premises servers and the SageMaker AI notebooks.

explanation: Amazon EFS provides a POSIX-compliant file system that supports file locking and can be mounted to both on-premises servers and SageMaker AI notebooks, making it suitable for shared data storage.

question: A company needs to analyze a large dataset stored in Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format. The company wants to use one-hot encoding for some columns and needs a no-code solution to transform the data. The solution must store the transformed data back to the same S3 bucket for model training. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Configure an AWS Glue DataBrew project that connects to the data. Use the DataBrew interactive interface to create a recipe that performs the one-hot encoding transformation. Create a job to apply the transformation and to write the output back to an S3 bucket.
mcqs.B: Configure an AWS Glue Data Catalog table that points to the data. Use Amazon Athena to write SQL commands to perform the one-hot encoding transformation. Configure Athena to write the query results back to an S3 bucket.
mcqs.C: Configure an AWS Glue Data Catalog table that points to the data. Create an AWS Glue ETL interactive notebook. Use the notebook to perform the one-hot encoding transformation. Run the configured cells and write the results back to an S3 bucket.
mcqs.D: Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster to access the data by using Redshift Spectrum. Use SQL commands to perform the one-hot encoding transformation within Amazon Redshift. Configure Amazon Redshift to write the results back to an S3 bucket.

explanation: AWS Glue DataBrew provides a no-code solution for data transformation. It supports one-hot encoding and can store transformed data back to S3.

question: A company wants to migrate ML models from an on-premises environment to Amazon SageMaker AI. The models are based on the PyTorch algorithm. The company needs to reuse its existing custom scripts as much as possible on AWS. Which feature of SageMaker AI should the company use to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: SageMaker AI built-in algorithms
mcqs.B: SageMaker Canvas
mcqs.C: SageMaker JumpStart
mcqs.D: SageMaker AI script mode

explanation: The company can use SageMaker AI script mode to reuse existing custom scripts. This feature allows for running custom algorithms and scripts on SageMaker.

question: A company uses an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to track the sale prices of sneakers over time. The dashboard aggregates sale prices scraped from many retail websites. The company wants to determine which prices are unusually high outliers and to display the outliers visually. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use a vertical bar chart to visualize the outliers. Use a calculated field in QuickSight to take the square roots of the outlier prices to generate the chart. Configure a custom AWS Lambda function to scan the data for anomalies.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to preprocess the data. Set the REMOVE_OUTLIERS operation to eliminate data rows that include unusually high prices. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to store the removed rows in Amazon DynamoDB.
mcqs.C: Use a vertical bar chart to visualize the outliers. Use a calculated field in QuickSight to square the outlier prices to generate the chart. Use QuickSight anomaly detection insights to determine which prices are unusually high.
mcqs.D: Use a QuickSight filter to find the lowest 10 values for sneaker price. Assign a specific color to the 10 lowest values.

explanation: QuickSight's anomaly detection can identify outliers, and using a calculated field to square prices can help visualize them effectively.

question: An ML engineer is using Amazon QuickSight anomaly detection to detect very high or very low machine operating temperatures compared to normal. The ML engineer sets the Severity parameter to Low and above. The ML engineer sets the Direction parameter to All. What effect will the ML engineer observe in the anomaly detection results if the ML engineer changes the Direction parameter to Lower than expected?

mcqs.A: Increased anomaly identification frequency and increased recall
mcqs.B: Decreased anomaly identification frequency and decreased recall
mcqs.C: Increased anomaly identification frequency and decreased recall
mcqs.D: Decreased anomaly identification frequency and increased recall

explanation: Changing the Direction parameter to Lower than expected will only detect anomalies that are lower than expected, reducing the overall anomaly identification frequency and decreasing recall.

question: A company runs its ML workflows on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. The ML workflows include ML services that perform training and inferences for ML models. Each ML service runs from its own standalone Docker image. The company needs to perform a lift and shift from the on-premises Kubernetes cluster to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Redesign the ML services to be configured in Kubeflow. Deploy the new Kubeflow managed ML services to the EKS cluster.
mcqs.B: Upload the Docker images to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Configure a deployment pipeline to deploy the images to the EKS cluster.
mcqs.C: Migrate the training data to an Amazon Redshift cluster. Retrain the models from the migrated training data by using Amazon Redshift ML. Deploy the retrained models to the EKS cluster.
mcqs.D: Configure an Amazon SageMaker AI notebook. Retrain the models with the same code. Deploy the retrained models to the EKS cluster.

explanation: Uploading Docker images to Amazon ECR and deploying them to EKS via a pipeline requires minimal changes to existing workflows, thus having the least operational overhead.

question: A retail company is creating an AI-powered assistant for customers. The company has a large body of documentation that the assistant needs to use for general inquiries. The company wants any responses about prices to use only documentation that is less than 1 month old. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Q Business to develop the responses. Configure a document attribute filter so that responses about prices use only the documents from the past month.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon Q Business to develop the responses. Configure the source attribution citation so that responses about prices use only the documents from the past month.
mcqs.C: Segment the documents into folders based on the month of document creation. Configure Amazon Q Developer to use only the documents from the past month to develop responses about prices.
mcqs.D: Segment the documents into folders based on the month of document creation. Grant the assistant access to only the documents from the past month for responses about prices. Use Amazon Q Developer to develop the responses.

explanation: Amazon Q Business can filter documents based on attributes, allowing for time-based filtering. This meets the requirement of using documentation less than 1 month old for price responses.

question: A travel company wants to create an ML model to recommend the next airport destination for its users. The company has collected millions of data records about user location, recent search history on the company's website, and 2,000 available airports. The data has several categorical features with a target column that is expected to have a high-dimensional sparse matrix. The company needs to use Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithms for the model. An ML engineer converts the categorical features by using one-hot encoding. Which algorithm should the ML engineer implement to meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use the CatBoost algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
mcqs.B: Use the DeepAR forecasting algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
mcqs.C: Use the Factorization Machines algorithm to recommend the next airport destination.
mcqs.D: Use the k-means algorithm to cluster users into groups. Map each group to the next airport destination based on user search history.

explanation: The Factorization Machines algorithm is suitable for high-dimensional sparse data and can handle categorical features converted using one-hot encoding, making it ideal for this recommendation task.

question: An ML engineer is configuring auto scaling for an inference component of a model that runs behind an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. The ML engineer configures SageMaker AI auto scaling with a target tracking scaling policy set to 100 invocations per model per minute. The SageMaker AI endpoint scales appropriately during normal business hours. However, the ML engineer notices that at the start of each business day, there are zero instances available to handle requests, which causes delays in processing. The ML engineer must ensure that the SageMaker AI endpoint can handle incoming requests at the start of each business day. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Reduce the SageMaker AI auto scaling cooldown period to the minimum supported value. Add an auto scaling lifecycle hook to scale the SageMaker AI instances.
mcqs.B: Change the target metric to CPU utilization.
mcqs.C: Modify the scaling policy target value to one.
mcqs.D: Apply a step scaling policy that scales based on an Amazon CloudWatch alarm. Apply a second CloudWatch alarm and scaling policy to scale the minimum number of instances from zero to one at the start of each business day.

explanation: The solution requires ensuring instances are available at the start of each business day. Option D directly addresses this by scaling the minimum number of instances from zero to one at the start of each business day using CloudWatch alarms and scaling policies.

question: An ML engineer is using an Amazon SageMaker Studio notebook to train a neural network by creating an estimator. The estimator runs a Python training script that uses Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) on a single instance that has more than one GPU. The ML engineer discovers that the training script is underutilizing GPU resources. The ML engineer must identify the point in the training script where resource utilization can be optimized. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to create a report that describes GPU utilization over time.
mcqs.B: Add SageMaker Profiler annotations to the training script. Run the script and generate a report from the results.
mcqs.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to create a report that describes GPU utilization and GPU memory utilization over time.
mcqs.D: Create a default monitor in Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor and suggest a baseline. Generate a report based on the constraints and statistics the monitor generates.

explanation: SageMaker Profiler helps identify performance bottlenecks in training scripts by collecting system and framework metrics. Adding profiler annotations allows detailed analysis of resource utilization.

question: A company is developing an internal cost-estimation tool that uses an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. Users upload high-resolution images to the tool. The model must process each image and predict the cost of the object in the image. The model also must notify the user when processing is complete. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use batch transform jobs for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to notify users.
mcqs.B: Store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use an asynchronous inference strategy for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify users.
mcqs.C: Store the images in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use batch transform jobs for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to notify users.
mcqs.D: Store the images in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the model on SageMaker AI. Use an asynchronous inference strategy for model inference. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify users.

explanation: Asynchronous inference strategy in SageMaker is suitable for processing high-resolution images and notifying users upon completion. This approach allows for processing large payloads and sending notifications via Amazon SNS.

question: A healthcare company uses an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint to host a model that predicts patient readmission risk to hospitals. The company wants to predict patient readmissions with high accuracy and is willing to tolerate false positives. The current model performance has degraded over the previous year. The company trains and deploys a new model as a shadow variant for testing on live traffic from hospitals. The company monitors the performance of the new model for a month. During the month of testing, the shadow variant has a higher recall than the existing model but has a lower precision. What should the company do next?

mcqs.A: Promote the shadow variant to full production.
mcqs.B: Extend the shadow testing period to capture more data. Monitor the new model to determine whether precision improves.
mcqs.C: Use a blue/green deployment strategy to allocate a small percentage of traffic to the shadow variant to reduce model errors.
mcqs.D: Disable the shadow variant and roll back to the main variant.

explanation: The company wants to predict patient readmissions with high accuracy and is willing to tolerate false positives. The new model has a higher recall, which aligns with the company's goal. Although it has a lower precision, promoting the shadow variant to full production is the best course of action given the company's priorities.

question: An airline company uses an ML model to adjust ticket prices based on demand. The model runs on Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoints. During previous deployments, the model failed to scale quickly enough when website traffic increased, which caused delays in price adjustments. An ML engineer needs to configure auto scaling for the SageMaker endpoints to respond rapidly to traffic changes. The solution must use target tracking scaling policies. Which configuration will be MOST responsive to sudden changes in traffic?

mcqs.A: Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker AI InvocationsPerInstance standard metric. Configure 10-second interval resolution, and set the default 300-second scale-in cooldown period.
mcqs.B: Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker AI InvocationsPerInstance metric. Configure high-resolution 10-second intervals, and set a 600-second scale-in cooldown period.
mcqs.C: Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker InvocationsPerInstance standard metric. Configure 10-second intervals resolution, and set a 600-second scale-in cooldown period.
mcqs.D: Configure auto scaling based on the SageMaker InvocationsPerInstance metric. Configure high-resolution 10-second intervals, and set the default 300-second scale-in cooldown period.

explanation: High-resolution metrics and a shorter cooldown period allow for more rapid responses to traffic changes. Option D combines these features.

question: An ML engineer is collecting data to train a classification ML model by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The target column can have two possible values: Class A or Class B. The ML engineer wants to ensure that the number of samples for both Class A and Class B are balanced, without losing any existing training data. The ML engineer must test the balance of the training data. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is equal to 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Clarify to check for class imbalance (CI). If the value is greater than 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance the classes.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is greater than 0, then use random undersampling in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.
mcqs.D: Use SageMaker JumpStart to generate a class imbalance (CI) report. If the value is equal to 0, then use synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Studio to balance the classes.

explanation: The ML engineer should use SageMaker Clarify to detect class imbalance and SMOTE in SageMaker Data Wrangler to balance classes without losing data.

question: An ML engineer is building a logistic regression model to predict customer churn for subscription services. The ML engineer is using a dataset that contains two string variables: location and job_seniority_level. The location variable has 3 distinct values, and the job_seniority_level variable has over 10 distinct values. The ML engineer must perform preprocessing on the variables. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Apply tokenization to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level.
mcqs.B: Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply ordinal encoding to job_seniority_level.
mcqs.C: Apply binning to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.
mcqs.D: Apply one-hot encoding to location. Apply standard scaling to job_seniority_level.

explanation: One-hot encoding is suitable for categorical variables with a small number of distinct values like location. Ordinal encoding is suitable for job_seniority_level with over 10 distinct values, assuming an order or hierarchy exists.

question: A company needs to deploy a custom-trained classification ML model on AWS. The model must make near real-time predictions with low latency and must handle variable request volumes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Create an Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform job to process inference requests in batches.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon API Gateway to receive prediction requests. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host and serve the model.
mcqs.C: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. Configure auto scaling for the endpoint.
mcqs.D: Launch AWS Deep Learning AMIs (DLAMI) on two Amazon EC2 instances. Run the instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

explanation: SageMaker real-time endpoints provide synchronous, low-latency inference with auto scaling.

question: A company runs a neural network model and retrains the model when the performance degrades. The company uses a training job that uses Amazon SageMaker AI distributed data parallelism (DDP). The training job takes several hours to run. The company wants to decrease the required time for the training job. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Increase the number of epochs.
mcqs.B: Increase the number of neurons in the hidden layers.
mcqs.C: Increase the number of layers.
mcqs.D: Increase the number of instances.

explanation: Increasing the number of instances will allow for more parallel processing, reducing the training time. This is because distributed data parallelism (DDP) splits the data across multiple instances, speeding up the training process.

question: An ML engineer needs to build a processing pipeline to identify and remove personally identifiable information (PII) from petabytes of unstructured data. The ML engineer will use the processed data to train ML models in Amazon SageMaker AI. Which solution will meet these requirements?

mcqs.A: Use the Apache Spark-based serverless engine from AWS Glue interactive sessions. Use the Detect PII transform feature to identify and remove the PII data.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue Data Wrangler within Amazon SageMaker Canvas to detect and remove the PII.
mcqs.C: Use the Amazon SageMaker Clarify API to detect and mask the PII data.
mcqs.D: Use the DetectEntities API action in Amazon Comprehend to identify and remove the PII data.

explanation: AWS Glue's Detect PII transform feature can identify and remove PII data from unstructured data, making it suitable for preparing data for ML model training in Amazon SageMaker.

question: A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to create a classification model to categorize the company's sales performance for each month of the previous 20 years on a scale from 1 to 5. The dataset includes fields for month, sales region, regional aggregate sales, and the number of stores in each sales region. The company notices that during two months of every year, the aggregate sales values are unexpectedly high. The company performs one-hot encoding on all non-numerical features in the training and validation datasets. The company uses the training dataset to train the classification model. When the company evaluates the model against the validation dataset, the results are less accurate than expected. The company must improve the model's accuracy on the validation dataset. Which solution will meet this requirement?

mcqs.A: Remove records that include outliers across all features.
mcqs.B: Use a stratified split on the month and sales region features.
mcqs.C: Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature.
mcqs.D: Perform normalization on the aggregate sales feature for each sales region.

explanation: Stratified splitting ensures representative samples from each time period and region.

question: A data scientist needs a highly available, scalable network file system that supports features like snapshots, cloning, and automated tiering for a large ML dataset. Which AWS storage service best meets these requirements?

mcqs.A: Amazon S3 with Lifecycle Policies
mcqs.B: Amazon EFS
mcqs.C: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
mcqs.D: Amazon FSx for Lustre

explanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides enterprise NAS features including snapshots, cloning, and automated tiering.

question: An ML pipeline requires ingesting streaming data into Amazon S3 with minimal setup and overhead. Which AWS service provides a fully managed way to do this, handling automatic scaling, buffering, and optional compression/encryption?

mcqs.A: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
mcqs.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose (now Amazon Data Firehose)
mcqs.C: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK)
mcqs.D: AWS DataSync

explanation: Amazon Data Firehose is a fully managed service that auto-scales to match data throughput and delivers to S3 with optional batching, compression, and encryption.

question: A team is building ML models that reuse many features (e.g. customer age, account status) across multiple projects. They want a central, managed repository to store, share, and retrieve these features for both training (batch) and online inference.

mcqs.A: Amazon DynamoDB
mcqs.B: AWS Glue Data Catalog
mcqs.C: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
mcqs.D: Amazon Redshift

explanation: SageMaker Feature Store provides a centralized repository with both online and offline stores for consistent feature values across training and inference.

question: A company needs to create a labeled image dataset by having humans label millions of images (e.g. object bounding boxes). Which AWS service provides built-in workflows and workforce options (including Mechanical Turk) to efficiently label data for ML?

mcqs.A: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
mcqs.B: AWS Step Functions
mcqs.C: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) only
mcqs.D: AWS DataBrew

explanation: SageMaker Ground Truth provides built-in labeling workflows with workforce options including Mechanical Turk.

question: A data engineer wants to clean and normalize a large dataset with a visual, no-code interface, applying many predefined transformations (filter anomalies, format conversion, etc.). Which AWS service is best suited for this task?

mcqs.A: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler
mcqs.B: AWS Glue DataBrew
mcqs.C: Amazon EMR with Hadoop
mcqs.D: Amazon SageMaker Processing

explanation: AWS Glue DataBrew offers 250+ pre-built visual transformations for data cleaning and normalization without writing code.

question: A startup wants to add real-time image recognition of celebrities to its app but has very limited ML expertise. Which AWS service should they use to quickly identify celebrities in images?

mcqs.A: Amazon Rekognition
mcqs.B: Amazon SageMaker Training with a deep learning model
mcqs.C: Amazon Textract
mcqs.D: AWS Lambda with custom code

explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides pre-trained APIs for celebrity recognition. It enables image recognition features without any ML expertise.

question: A machine learning engineer runs frequent training jobs with similar configurations during iterative model tuning. They want to reduce the startup latency for each new job so that provisioned instances can be reused. Which SageMaker feature should they use?

mcqs.A: Multi-model endpoints
mcqs.B: SageMaker Training with Managed Spot Instances
mcqs.C: SageMaker Managed Warm Pools
mcqs.D: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling Groups

explanation: SageMaker managed warm pools retain provisioned instances between training jobs, reducing startup latency.

question: A neural network is overfitting the training data, with very low training loss but high validation loss. Which technique is most appropriate to reduce overfitting in the model?

mcqs.A: Increase the learning rate
mcqs.B: Add dropout layers or L2 regularization
mcqs.C: Remove batch normalization
mcqs.D: Use a smaller training dataset

explanation: Dropout and L2 regularization help reduce overfitting by preventing the model from relying too heavily on any single neuron or feature.

question: A data scientist wants to automatically find the best hyperparameters for their SageMaker training job without manually tuning. Which SageMaker feature should they use?

mcqs.A: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning (Hyperparameter Tuning Jobs)
mcqs.B: SageMaker Model Monitor
mcqs.C: AWS Batch
mcqs.D: SageMaker Pipelines

explanation: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning is used for hyperparameter optimization.

question: A company needs to deploy a trained deep learning model for inference on edge devices (e.g., mobile and IoT) with low latency. Which AWS service should they use to optimize and package the model for such devices?

mcqs.A: AWS IoT Greengrass
mcqs.B: Amazon SageMaker Neo
mcqs.C: Amazon EC2 GPU instances
mcqs.D: AWS Lambda

explanation: SageMaker Neo optimizes and packages models for edge devices.

question: An ML team wants to implement a CI/CD pipeline for their model training and deployment workflows using AWS developer tools. Which combination of AWS services would be most appropriate for version control and automated deployment?

mcqs.A: AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeCommit/CodeBuild/CodeDeploy
mcqs.B: Amazon SageMaker Processing and Amazon QuickSight
mcqs.C: AWS Step Functions and Amazon CloudWatch Events
mcqs.D: AWS DataPipeline and AWS Batch

explanation: AWS CodePipeline with CodeCommit, CodeBuild, and CodeDeploy provides a complete CI/CD solution for version control and automated deployment.

question: A deployed SageMaker endpoint is experiencing increased traffic. To handle this, which feature should be configured to automatically scale the number of inference instances based on utilization?

mcqs.A: SageMaker Endpoint Auto Scaling with target tracking (e.g., CPU utilization)
mcqs.B: AWS Lambda concurrency settings
mcqs.C: Amazon CloudFront with caching
mcqs.D: AWS Elastic Load Balancer (ELB)

explanation: SageMaker endpoint auto scaling uses target tracking policies to automatically add or remove instances based on demand.

question: After deploying a model to production, you want to automatically detect when incoming data distributions change significantly (data drift). Which Amazon SageMaker feature is designed for monitoring such data and model quality in real time?

mcqs.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
mcqs.B: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
mcqs.C: SageMaker Clarify (after training)
mcqs.D: Amazon Inspector

explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor detects data drift and model quality degradation in real-time.

question: A company wants to reduce costs on SageMaker training and inference. Which of the following AWS purchasing options can significantly lower compute costs if the workload is flexible and can tolerate interruptions?

mcqs.A: AWS Reserved Instances and SageMaker Savings Plans
mcqs.B: Provisioned Instances only
mcqs.C: AWS Spot Instances
mcqs.D: Pre-paid monthly flat-rate SageMaker license

explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings for interruptible workloads. ML training jobs with checkpointing can tolerate Spot interruptions and resume training.

question: What is the best practice to secure access to your SageMaker resources (models, data) and ensure that only authorized entities can access them?

mcqs.A: Configure IAM roles and policies with the principle of least privilege for all ML resources.
mcqs.B: Always use root AWS credentials for SageMaker operations.
mcqs.C: Disable Amazon VPC and security groups so the model is public.
mcqs.D: Store all model artifacts in an unencrypted S3 bucket.

explanation: Using IAM roles and policies with least-privilege access ensures only authorized users and services can access SageMaker resources. This approach is a foundation of AWS ML security.

question: A company stores historical data in .csv files in Amazon S3. Only some of the rows and columns in the .csv files are populated. The columns are not labeled. An ML engineer must prepare and store the data for ML training. Which combination of steps should the ML engineer take to prepare the data with the LEAST operational overhead?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon SageMaker batch transform for data cleaning, then store results in S3.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer schemas, then use AWS Glue DataBrew for data cleaning and feature engineering, then store the resulting data in Amazon S3.
mcqs.C: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to visualize the data, then use SageMaker Processing for cleaning, then store in Amazon Redshift.
mcqs.D: Manually inspect the CSV files in a notebook, label columns by hand, and upload cleaned files to S3.

explanation: AWS Glue crawlers infer schemas automatically and AWS Glue DataBrew provides no-code data cleaning, making option B the most efficient.

question: An ML engineer is preparing a regression model for home prices. The features include Price, Date Sold, Neighborhood (categorical), Square Footage, and Latitude/Longitude. Which set of preprocessing techniques is MOST appropriate for Price, Date Sold, and Neighborhood respectively?

mcqs.A: Price: Logarithmic Transformation, Date Sold: Feature Splitting (year/month), Neighborhood: One-hot Encoding
mcqs.B: Price: Standardization, Date Sold: One-hot Encoding, Neighborhood: Logarithmic Transformation
mcqs.C: Price: Min-Max Scaling, Date Sold: Label Encoding, Neighborhood: Normalization
mcqs.D: Price: One-hot Encoding, Date Sold: Logarithmic Transformation, Neighborhood: Feature Splitting

explanation: Log-transform normalizes right-skewed prices; feature-splitting extracts temporal patterns from dates; one-hot encoding converts nominal categories to binary vectors.

question: An ML engineer must unify transaction logs and customer profiles stored in Amazon S3 with on-premises MySQL data. The engineer needs a service that supports ingestion, cataloging, and integration from both cloud and on-premises sources with minimal operational overhead. Which AWS service is BEST suited?

mcqs.A: Amazon EMR Spark jobs
mcqs.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
mcqs.C: Amazon DynamoDB
mcqs.D: AWS Lake Formation

explanation: AWS Lake Formation provides a unified data lake for cloud and on-premises sources, handling ingestion, cataloging, and access control centrally.

question: An ML engineer is preprocessing data that contains many missing values and inconsistent formats before SageMaker training. The engineer needs a scalable, managed solution. What is the best practice?

mcqs.A: Drop all rows with any missing values to ensure clean data.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue jobs to clean, transform, and standardize the data at scale.
mcqs.C: Train the model with the raw data and let SageMaker handle missing values automatically.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Athena SQL queries to fix formatting issues in-place in S3.

explanation: AWS Glue provides a scalable, managed ETL service to handle data preprocessing tasks.

question: A fraud detection dataset has severe class imbalance (99.5% legitimate, 0.5% fraud). An ML engineer needs to balance the dataset with the LEAST operational effort. Which solution should the engineer use?

mcqs.A: Write a custom PySpark job on Amazon EMR to implement SMOTE.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Studio Classic built-in sampling functions.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew built-in features to oversample the minority class.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler's balance data operation to oversample the minority class.

explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler's balance data operation applies SMOTE or random oversampling via a visual interface, requiring the least operational effort.

question: An ecommerce application generates high-volume clickstream data. The data must be ingested, processed, and visualized in near real time. The solution must support SQL for data processing and Jupyter notebooks for interactive analysis. Which architecture meets these requirements?

mcqs.A: Amazon Data Firehose – AWS Lambda – Amazon S3 – Amazon QuickSight
mcqs.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams – Amazon Data Firehose – Amazon Athena – Amazon QuickSight
mcqs.C: Amazon MSK – AWS Glue with PySpark – Amazon S3 – Amazon QuickSight
mcqs.D: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams – Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (Studio Notebooks) – Amazon OpenSearch Service

explanation: Amazon Managed Flink Studio Notebooks support both streaming SQL and interactive Jupyter analysis on Kinesis streams, combining real-time processing with exploratory analytics.

question: An ML engineer needs to build data ingestion pipelines and ML model deployment pipelines. Raw data is stored in Amazon S3 in various formats. Which combination provides the BEST approach for batch ETL and ML orchestration?

mcqs.A: Amazon Data Firehose – SageMaker Studio Classic
mcqs.B: AWS Glue – SageMaker Studio Classic
mcqs.C: Amazon Redshift ML – SageMaker Studio Classic
mcqs.D: Amazon Athena – SageMaker notebook instances

explanation: AWS Glue provides serverless batch ETL for S3 data; SageMaker Studio provides the ML IDE for training and deployment – together they form a complete data-to-model pipeline.

question: An ML engineer must query thousands of CSV objects in a central Amazon S3 bucket, filtered by transaction date, with the LEAST operational overhead. Which approach should the engineer use?

mcqs.A: Use Amazon Athena with CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) to query and store results based on transaction date.
mcqs.B: Use AWS Glue ETL jobs to load data into Amazon Redshift Spectrum for querying.
mcqs.C: Use AWS Glue Spark jobs to query and store filtered results in a new S3 bucket.
mcqs.D: Use Amazon Data Firehose with AWS Lambda to filter and partition the data.

explanation: Athena CTAS queries S3 directly with serverless SQL, outputting filtered results back to S3 with the lowest overhead.

question: An ML engineer must use Amazon SageMaker Canvas with complex-structured data stored in Amazon S3. The engineer wants to minimize processing time when loading data. Which file format should the engineer use?

mcqs.A: CSV compressed with Snappy
mcqs.B: JSONL (JSON Lines)
mcqs.C: Apache Parquet
mcqs.D: TFRecord

explanation: Apache Parquet's columnar format provides faster reads and smaller storage, making it optimal for SageMaker Canvas.

question: In machine learning, the process of extracting useful information from existing raw data to create new predictive attributes is called:

mcqs.A: Feature Estimating
mcqs.B: Feature Engineering
mcqs.C: Feature Enablement
mcqs.D: Feature Evaluating

explanation: Feature engineering is the process of creating new predictive attributes from raw data to improve model performance.

question: An engineer needs to restrict access to an Amazon S3 bucket whose objects contain PII data labeled per marketing campaign. Each ML engineer should only see data from their assigned campaign. Which approach provides the MOST scalable, fine-grained access control?

mcqs.A: IAM policies on the AWS Glue Data Catalog restricting Amazon Athena access by campaign.
mcqs.B: Amazon DynamoDB Streams with AWS Lambda updating S3 bucket policies dynamically.
mcqs.C: AWS Lake Formation LF-Tags mapping engineers to their respective campaigns.
mcqs.D: S3 bucket policies with conditions filtered by campaign prefix.

explanation: Lake Formation LF-Tags enable attribute-based access control, dynamically mapping users to data partitions (campaigns) without creating individual IAM policies.

question: A company is training a fraud model on a dataset that contains categorical features (occupation, country) and numerical features (transaction amount). Most ML algorithms require numeric input. Which solution transforms categorical data into numerical data with the LEAST effort?

mcqs.A: Manually one-hot encode all categorical features in Jupyter notebooks.
mcqs.B: Train the algorithm directly on raw categorical data without encoding.
mcqs.C: Use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to transform categorical data into numerical data.
mcqs.D: Use Data Wrangler to transform numerical data into categorical data.

explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler provides built-in categorical encoders, converting categorical features to numeric with zero code.

question: A company uses Amazon SageMaker for experimentation, training, a central model registry, deployment, and monitoring. They need the central model registry to manage different versions of models with the LEAST operational overhead. Which approach should they use?

mcqs.A: Create a separate Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository for each model.
mcqs.B: Use Amazon ECR with unique tags for each model version.
mcqs.C: Use the SageMaker Model Registry with model groups to catalog the models.
mcqs.D: Use the SageMaker Model Registry with only unique tags for each model version.

explanation: SageMaker Model Registry with model groups provides built-in versioning and lifecycle management for ML models.

question: A company is running consecutive training jobs with similar configurations and wants to minimize infrastructure startup times between jobs. Which SageMaker feature should they use?

mcqs.A: Managed Spot Training
mcqs.B: SageMaker managed warm pools
mcqs.C: SageMaker Training Compiler
mcqs.D: SageMaker distributed data parallelism (SMDDP) library

explanation: SageMaker managed warm pools keep training instances provisioned between consecutive jobs, reducing startup time.

question: An ML engineer has trained a neural network using stochastic gradient descent (SGD). During training, both the training and validation loss oscillate significantly – decreasing and then increasing repeatedly. What should the engineer do to stabilize training?

mcqs.A: Introduce early stopping to halt training at the best validation loss.
mcqs.B: Increase the size of the test set.
mcqs.C: Increase the learning rate to converge faster.
mcqs.D: Decrease the learning rate to allow more stable convergence.

explanation: Oscillating loss during SGD training means the learning rate is too large; decreasing it allows smoother convergence.

question: A model's training accuracy is 98% but validation accuracy is only 72%. Which technique should be applied to address this issue?

mcqs.A: Increase the number of training epochs
mcqs.B: Use a more complex model architecture
mcqs.C: Apply L1 or L2 regularization to the model
mcqs.D: Reduce the validation set size

explanation: This is a classic case of overfitting. L1/L2 regularization reduces model complexity and improves generalization.

question: A team wants automatic algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization for a recommendation system. The training data is stored in Amazon S3. Which SageMaker feature provides this end-to-end AutoML capability?

mcqs.A: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
mcqs.B: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
mcqs.C: Amazon SageMaker Processing
mcqs.D: Amazon SageMaker Neo

explanation: SageMaker Autopilot automates the complete ML workflow, including data preprocessing, algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model ranking for tabular datasets stored in S3.

question: An ML engineer must fine-tune a large language model (LLM) for text summarization using a low-code/no-code (LCNC) approach in Amazon SageMaker. Which approach should the engineer use?

mcqs.A: Use SageMaker Studio to manually fine-tune on EC2 instances.
mcqs.B: Use SageMaker Autopilot to fine-tune via a custom API endpoint.
